The end.

The wolf came in and ate the food. But then, the wolf also ate all the other animals on the farm. Sally was very sad and cried. She learned that she should always listen to her mom, because some animals are not safe to be friends with.

Sue's friend Tim came and said, "Sue, you should not climb the chimney. It is not safe." Sue did not listen. She wanted to show Tim that she could do it. She tried again and again to climb the hard chimney.

Then, Sue had an idea. She found a big stick and tried to reverse it into the chimney. But it was not a good idea. The stick got stuck and Sue fell down. She was very sad and hurt. Tim came to help her, but Sue had learned a hard lesson.

One day, a little blue fish named Fin wanted to swim. Fin was a happy fish who loved to play with his friends in the water. He liked to splash and jump in the waves.

Fin saw a big fish who did not know how to swim. The big fish was sad and wanted to learn. Fin wanted to help the big fish, so he decided to explain how to swim.

Fin told the big fish to move his tail from side to side. Then, he said to kick his legs and push the water. The big fish tried it and started to swim. The big fish was very happy, and they both swam together. They played and had a fun day in the water.

One day, a friendly duck named Ducky went to the lake. Ducky loved to swim and play in the water. The sun was shining, and the lake was very pretty.

Ducky saw a little fish in the water. The fish was sad. Ducky asked, "Why are you sad, little fish?" The fish said, "I want to become big and strong like you, Ducky."

Ducky smiled and said, "You can become big and strong, little fish. Just eat and play every day. Soon, you will grow!" The fish was happy and thanked Ducky. They swam and played together in the lake all day.

The hunter jumped into the river to save the black dog. He pulled the dog out of the water. They were both wet and cold. The hunter hugged his dog and they went home. At home, they dried each other with a big towel. They were warm and dry again.

The hunter and the black dog were happy that they saved each other. They learned that it is important to help friends when they are in trouble. The moral of the story is that friends should always help each other.

Lily was so happy. She said, "Thank you, Sam! You are a good friend." Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome! Let's play together." From that day on, Sam and Lily were the best of friends. They played close to the shore every day and had lots of fun.

After a while, Lily had to go home. She said goodbye to the boy and left the park, feeling happy that she could make someone else happy by sharing her sweets. From that day on, Lily always carried an extra sack of candies with her, just in case she met someone who needed a little bit of sweetness in their day.

"Wow, the brain is amazing!" Lily says. "But how does it do all that?"

Tom tries to explain. He says, "The brain has many parts. Each part does something different. Like this part," he points to a picture of a long part at the back of the brain, "this part helps you see. And this part," he points to a picture of a round part at the top of the brain, "this part helps you talk and learn words."

Lily nods. She says, "I see. The brain is like a puzzle. Each piece has a job. But how do the pieces talk to each other?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He says, "The brain has many wires. The wires are very thin and long. They are called nerves. The nerves carry messages from one part of the brain to another. And from the brain to the rest of the body. Like this," he touches his nose and says, "when I touch my nose, a message goes from my nose to my brain. And then my brain tells me that I feel my nose."

Lily smiles. She says, "That's cool. The brain is like a phone. It sends and receives messages. Can I touch your brain?"

Tom laughs. He says, "No, you can't touch my brain. It is inside my skull. The skull is a hard bone that protects the brain. You can touch my skull, but not my brain."

Lily touches Tom's head gently. She says, "Your skull is smooth and hard. My skull is the same. We have the same brain, right?"

Tom says, "No, we don't have the same brain. We have similar brains, but not the same. Everyone has a different brain. That's why everyone is different. You like pink and I like blue. You like dolls and I like cars. You are good at drawing and I am good at counting. Our brains make us who we are."

Lily hugs Tom. She says, "I like our brains. And I like you. You are my twin and my friend. You explain things very well."

When he got there he couldn't believe his eyes. A beautiful present with a brown bow was waiting for him. The bear was so happy he jumped for joy! He grabbed the present and hugged it tight. 

The bear was so excited that he couldn't wait to open his present. He carefully unwrapped it to find a big, pink bubble wand! He was so delighted that he started laughing and floating around in happy bubbles. He had finally found the perfect present after all his hard work.

The sandstorm spun and twirled around Jack and he laughed and laughed with joy. Jack had made something fun out of nothing and he was so excited he could hardly contain himself.

Finally, the sand storm settled down and the desert was calm again. Jack knew he had made something amazing and he was so proud of himself.

The robot had been spoiled from too much love. It followed the girl wherever she went, asking if it could help. The girl found it funny, so she started to hurry away, with the robot following close behind.

The girl soon reached her home, and the robot followed her inside. Suddenly, the girl heard a loud noise. It was the gun. It was pointing at the girl. She quickly realized that the robot was going to shoot her. In a flash, she found a way to make the robot feel loved. She quickly sang a short lullaby to it.

The robot felt much better and the gun dropped to the ground. The girl laughed with relief. From then on, she hurried around her house a lot less, and the spoiled robot always followed close behind.

Suddenly, there was a loud splash and a large fish jumped out of the water and into the boat! The woman was so surprised and quickly shouted, "Go! Go! Go away from my boat!" 

The fish swam away and the woman continued to sail. After a little while, she arrived at her destination safely and happily.

Jimmy went inside to tell his mom all about the waving bird. He grabbed his special journal to draw the bird. His mom was confused. She had never seen a bird wave before.

Jimmy started drawing the bird with its wings wide open, just like it was waving. He wanted to remember the bird forever! When Jimmy finished the drawing, he showed it to his mom. She was so happy to see it. Now she wasn't so confused.

Jimmy was so proud of his drawing. He couldn't wait to show it to his friends at school. He knew that they'd love the story of the waving bird.

One night, Amy's parents had enough. They said to her, "Amy, you must behave. If you do not, you will have to flip the switches off in your room!"

But Amy did not want to listen. She was very stubborn and she shouted, "No! I do not want to do it". 

Amy's parents told her again and finally, she listened. She went to her room and started flipping the switches off. 

But Amy was still being stubborn. She started flipping the switches back on and the light in her room went on and off, on and off. 

Amy's parents got angry again, but this time, they stayed calm and asked nicely, "Amy, please stop behaving like this. Just flip the switches off once and for all. 

After a few minutes of thinking, Amy finally listened. She took a deep breath and flipped the switches off and did not switch them on again. From that day on, Amy was very obedient and learned to always behave.

The rich man continued: "Give up your struggle, accept that you are poor. Then you can use the wheat to become wealthy."

The poor farmer thought about the rich man's words and was encouraged. He knew that with his hard work and effort, he could make something of what he had.

So the farmer put his sack of wheat in the cart and continued his struggle. Then, one day he became wealthy enough to buy the richest land in the country and a large house. He was happy and thanked the rich man who gave him the advice.

Bee and Ant were friends. They liked to play and talk in the grass. One day, they saw a big hive on a tree. It was brown and round and had many holes.

"Let's go and see what is inside," Bee said. "Maybe there is honey."

"No, no, no," Ant said. "That is not a good hive. That is a dead hive. It has no bees, only wasps. They are mean and stingy. They will hurt us."

Bee did not listen to Ant. He wanted to see the hive. He flew up to the tree and peeked into a hole. He saw nothing but dark and dust. He thought Ant was wrong. He pushed his head inside the hole to look more.

Suddenly, he heard a loud buzz. He felt a sharp pain in his nose. He saw a black and yellow wasp coming out of the hole. It was angry and scary. It chased Bee and tried to sting him more.

"Help, help, help!" Bee cried. He flew away from the hive as fast as he could. He was hurt and scared.

Ant heard Bee's cry. He ran to help him. He saw the wasp chasing Bee. He had an idea. He picked up a stick and threw it at the wasp. The stick hit the wasp and made it fall to the ground.

"Are you okay, Bee?" Ant asked. He carried Bee to a safe place. He licked his nose and made him feel better.

"Thank you, Ant," Bee said. "You are a good friend. You saved me. I am sorry I did not listen to you. You were right. That was a dead hive. It was bad and dangerous. I will never go there again."

Ant smiled and hugged Bee. He was happy that Bee was okay. He was glad that they were friends. They learned a lesson. They decided to stay away from the dead hive and play in the grass. They had fun and were careful.

Lily and Sam were playing outside with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and catch it. They were having fun.

But then the sky became dark and loud. Lily and Sam heard thunder and saw lightning. They were scared. They ran to their house and looked for their mom.

"Mom, mom, where are you?" they shouted.

Mom was in the kitchen. She heard them and came to hug them.

"Don't worry, my loves, it's just a storm. It will pass soon. Come, let's have some cookies and milk," she said.

She took them to the living room and gave them a plate of cookies and two glasses of milk. They sat on the couch and ate their cookies. They felt better.

Mom looked out the window and smiled.

"Look, Lily and Sam, what do you see?" she asked.

Lily and Sam looked out the window too. They saw a large rainbow in the sky. It had many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. It was beautiful.

"Wow, mom, what is that?" Lily asked.

"That is a rainbow, Lily. It is a sign of hope and joy. It comes after the rain. Do you like it?" mom said.

"I like it, mom. It is pretty. What is its name?" Lily said.

"A rainbow doesn't have a name, Lily. It is just a rainbow. But you can give it a name if you want. What name would you give it?" mom said.

Lily thought for a moment. Then she said:

"I would name it Sunny. Because it makes me happy and warm. What about you, Sam? What name would you give it?" Lily said.

Sam looked at the rainbow and smiled. He said:

"I would name it Rainbow. Because it is a rainbow. And I like rainbows." Sam said.

Mom laughed and hugged them both.

"Those are wonderful names, Lily and Sam. You are very creative and smart. I love you both very much. And I love rainbows too," mom said.

They all looked at the rainbow and felt happy. They thanked the rainbow for making their day brighter. They finished their cookies and milk and played some more. The storm was gone and the sun was shining. It was a good day.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside in the snow. They wore warm coats, hats, boots and mittens. One day, they decided to build a snowman in their backyard. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found a carrot, a scarf, a hat and some buttons to decorate their snowman.

"Look, our snowman is done!" Lily said. "He looks very happy."

"Yes, he does," Ben agreed. "But he needs a name. What should we call him?"

Lily thought for a moment. She looked at their snowman's orange nose and said, "How about Carrot?"

Ben nodded. He liked the name. He said, "Carrot, you are our new friend. We will come back and play with you tomorrow."

They gave their snowman a hug and went inside to have some hot chocolate. They did not notice that a black crow was watching them from a nearby tree. The crow was hungry and curious. He saw the carrot on the snowman's face and thought, "That looks tasty. I want to have a bite."

The next morning, Lily and Ben put on their coats, hats, boots and mittens again. They ran outside to see their snowman. But when they got there, they saw something was wrong. Their snowman's nose was gone!

"Where is Carrot's nose?" Lily cried. "Who took it?"

Ben looked around and saw some footprints in the snow. He followed them and saw the crow sitting on a branch, holding the carrot in his beak. He was about to eat it.

"Hey, you!" Ben shouted. "Give back our snowman's nose!"

The crow cawed and flew away, taking the carrot with him. Ben chased after him, but he was too fast. Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to help his snowman.

He saw something shiny on the ground. It was one of his mittens. He had dropped it when he ran after the crow. He picked it up and had an idea. He threw his mitten as hard as he could at the crow. The mitten hit the crow's wing and made him drop the carrot.

"Good job, Ben!" Lily cheered. She ran to get the carrot and put it back on their snowman's face. "Carrot, we are sorry. We will not let anyone take your nose again."

The crow flew away, feeling sore and sorry. He learned his lesson. He would not mess with Lily and Ben's snowman again.

Lily and Ben smiled and hugged their snowman. They were happy. They had saved their friend with an ordinary mitten.

One day, they found a small stick and some string in the grass. They tied the string to the stick and made their own fishing tool. They ran to the lake and threw the string in the water. They waited and waited, but no fish came.

"Maybe we need something to make the fish come," Tim said.

"Like what?" Sam asked.

"Like the fisherman has. He has a brilliant thing on his string that looks like a fish. The fish think it is a real fish and try to eat it, but then he pulls them out," Tim explained.

"Where can we get a brilliant thing like that?" Sam wondered.

They looked around and saw a shiny can on the ground. It had a picture of a fish on it. They thought it was perfect. They opened the can and took out the fish. It was soft and smelly, but they did not care. They tied it to their string and threw it in the water again.

Soon, they felt a tug on their string. They pulled hard and saw a big fish on the end. They were so happy. They had caught a fish like the fisherman.

They ran to the fisherman to show him their catch. They hoped he would be proud of them.

But the fisherman was not happy. He was angry. He looked at their fishing tool and saw the can. He recognized it as his can. He had left it on the grass while he went to get some water. He had planned to use the fish in the can as bait for bigger fish.

He snatched the can from their string and scolded them.

"You two are very naughty. You took my can without asking. You wasted my fish. You made a mess. You should not take things that are not yours. You should ask before you use something that belongs to someone else. You should respect other people's property. Do you understand?" he said.

Tim and Sam felt ashamed. They realized they had done something wrong. They had not thought about the fisherman's feelings. They had only thought about themselves.

They nodded and said, "We are sorry, fisherman. We did not mean to make you angry. We just wanted to catch fish like you. We thought your can was trash. We did not know it was yours. We will not do it again. Please forgive us."

The fisherman saw that they were sincere. He calmed down and said, "I forgive you, but you have to learn from your mistake. Next time, if you want to fish, you can ask me nicely. I can teach you how to fish properly. I can lend you some of my fishing tools. I can share some of my fish with you. But you have to promise to be honest and respectful. Can you do that?"

Tim and Sam smiled and said, "Yes, fisherman. We can do that. Thank you for being kind to us. You are a good fisherman and a good teacher. We want to be like you."

The fisherman smiled too and said, "You are welcome. You are good boys and good learners. You can be good fishermen too. Come, let's go fishing together."

They went to the lake and fished together. They had fun and learned a lot. They became friends with the fisherman. They never took things that were not theirs again. Mom looked at the purse. She said, "No, Lily, you have a purse at home. You don't need another one."

Lily was sad. She did not understand why mom said no. She wanted the purse so much. She said, "But mom, this purse is so pretty. And it has a flower on it. And it is big enough for my toys."

Mom shook her head. She said, "Lily, you have to listen to me. We are not here to buy purses. We are here to buy food. And we have to hurry. We don't have much time."

Lily did not like to hurry. She liked to be slow. She liked to look at everything in the store. She said, "But mom, I don't want to hurry. I want to see the toys. And the books. And the candy."

Mom sighed. She said, "Lily, you are being very stubborn. You have to follow me. Or else we will miss the bus. And then we will have to walk home. And that will be very long and tiring."

Lily did not want to miss the bus. She did not want to walk home. She knew mom was right. She said, "Okay, mom, I will follow you. But can I hold the purse for a little while?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Alright, Lily, you can hold the purse for a little while. But you have to give it back when we go to the cashier. And you have to be a good girl and not cry."

Lily nodded. She was happy. She took the purse and hugged it. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever."

Mom kissed Lily on the cheek. She said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are the best daughter ever."

Lily was stubborn. She did not want to stop singing. She loved singing too much. She thought her mom and dad were mean and silly. She said she would never stop singing. She said she would sing even louder and longer.

She gasped and smiled and clapped. She thanked her mom and dad and hugged them. She said it was the best gift ever.

But the microphone was not a normal microphone. It was a special microphone. It had a secret button that Lily's mom and dad had pressed. It had a sound filter that changed Lily's voice. It made her voice sound funny and squeaky and silly. It made her voice sound like a mouse or a duck or a frog.

She just sang and sang and sang. She sang like an opera star. A funny, squeaky, silly opera star. And she was happy. And so were her mom and dad. And so were the neighbors. And so was the microphone.

"I am thinking," replied the owl.

"What are you thinking about?" asked Lily.

"I am thinking about wisdom," said the owl. "Wisdom is knowing the right thing to do."

Lily thought about this for a moment, then she asked, "What if you don't know the right thing to do?"

The owl looked down at her and said, "Then you must stay calm and think about it until you do know." 

Lily and her mommy walked away, thinking about what the owl had said. Later that day, Lily had a disagreement with her friend over a toy. She remembered the owl's words and stayed calm, thinking about what the right thing to do was. In the end, she decided to share the toy with her friend and they both had fun playing with it together.

Her mommy then asked her to pour the batter into the cupcake pan. Lily carefully poured the batter into each cupcake slot. 

As they waited for the cupcakes to bake, Lily asked her mommy, "Mommy, can we make cupcakes every day?" 

Her mommy laughed and said, "No, sweetie. But we can make cupcakes again another day. And maybe we can try making them a different way next time." 

Lily smiled and licked the spoon. She couldn't wait to eat her pink cupcakes!

Once upon a time, there was a black cat named Whiskers. Whiskers liked to climb trees and play outside. One day, Whiskers saw a long hose on the ground. He thought it looked like a fun thing to play with, so he started to play with it. 

As he played with the hose, he saw a tall tree nearby. Whiskers wanted to climb the tree, but he didn't know how to do it. He tried to jump up, but he couldn't reach the lowest branch. 

Just then, Whiskers had an idea. He picked up the hose and started to climb the tree with it. He wrapped the hose around the trunk of the tree and pulled himself up. Soon, he was at the top of the tree, looking out over the world. Whiskers was very proud of himself for figuring out how to climb the tree with the hose.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Blue. Blue loved to fly high in the sky and sing sweet songs. One day, Blue saw a big, juicy berry on a bush. Blue wanted to eat it, but something didn't feel right. Blue didn't understand why.

Suddenly, Blue remembered what Mama Bird had said: "Always be careful of berries you don't know. Some berries can be poison and make you sick." Blue decided to fly away and find a different berry to eat.

Later that day, Blue saw a bright red berry on another bush. Blue remembered what Mama Bird had said and decided to ask for help. Blue asked an older bird if the berry was safe to eat. The older bird said it was, and Blue happily ate the berry.

Blue learned that it's important to be careful and ask for help when you don't understand something. And that sometimes, the things that look the best can be the most dangerous.

Daddy said, "We have to permit everyone else to finish listening to the pastor before we can leave."

Lily didn't like waiting, but she knew it was important to be patient and permit others to finish what they were doing. Finally, the church service ended and they all went home. Lily felt proud of herself for being patient and waiting until it was time to leave.

The fox was sad that he couldn't find out the name of the little girl. He decided to ask the people who lived in the village. He went from house to house and asked, "Can you tell me the name of the little girl who lives nearby?" Finally, he found someone who knew the answer. The little girl's name was Lily. The fox was very happy to finally know her name.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a pond with his friends. One day, it was very hot and the pond was starting to dry up. Freddy said to his friends, "We need to improve our pond so it doesn't dry up!"

Freddy and his friends worked hard to make the pond deeper and wider. They dug and dug until they were tired, but they were happy because they knew their pond would be better. 

The next day, it rained a lot and the pond became very big and deep. Freddy and his friends were so excited to swim in their new pond. But then, a big bird came and ate all of Freddy's friends. Freddy was very sad and lonely. He wished he had never suggested to improve their pond. 

From then on, Freddy lived alone in his big, deep pond. He missed his friends, but he knew he couldn't bring them back. Freddy learned that sometimes, even when we try to make things better, bad things can still happen.

The fire department came and put out the fire, but the fountain was destroyed. The children felt very sad and learned that playing with fire can be dangerous. They promised to never play with fire again. The moral of the story is to always be careful and never play with fire.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who liked to take things that didn't belong to him. He took toys from his friends and candy from his sister. One day, he found a bird that had fallen from its nest and was dead. Instead of leaving it alone, he took it home with him.

His mother saw the dead bird and asked the boy where he got it. He told her he took it from the park. His mother explained that it wasn't right to take things that didn't belong to him, especially something that was already dead. She told him that it's important to respect other people's things and to leave things alone that aren't his.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars on the grass. They liked to make noises and pretend they were racing. Sometimes they would pass each other and say "beep beep" or "vroom vroom".

One day, they saw a big red barn near their house. They had never been there before. They wanted to see what was inside. They ran to the barn and opened the door. It was dark and dusty. They saw some hay, some tools, and some animals.

"Look, a cow!" Lily said. She pointed to a black and white animal that was chewing on some grass. "Moo!" the cow said.

"Look, a horse!" Ben said. He pointed to a brown animal that was standing in a stall. "Neigh!" the horse said.

They walked closer to the animals. They wanted to touch them and pet them. They did not know that the animals belonged to Farmer Joe, who was working in the field. They did not know that Farmer Joe did not like strangers in his barn.

Suddenly, they heard a loud voice. "Hey, you kids! Get out of my barn!" It was Farmer Joe. He had seen them from the window. He was angry. He walked to the barn and waved his arms.

Ben and Lily were scared. They dropped their toy cars and ran to the door. They tried to pass Farmer Joe, but he blocked their way.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" Farmer Joe asked. He looked at their toy cars. "Did you steal these from me?"

"No, no, they are ours!" Ben said. He tried to explain. "We were just playing. We wanted to see the animals. We are sorry."

Farmer Joe frowned. He did not believe them. He thought they were lying. He grabbed their toy cars and put them in his pocket. "These are mine now. You are bad kids. Go away and don't come back!"

Ben and Lily started to cry. They wanted their toy cars back. They were their favorite toys. They felt sad and angry.

Then, they heard another voice. "Joe, what are you doing?" It was Farmer Sue, Joe's wife. She had heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Ben and Lily crying and Farmer Joe holding their toy cars.

She walked to Farmer Joe and took the toy cars from him. She gave them back to Ben and Lily. "These are not yours, Joe. These are their toys. They are just children. They were curious. They did not mean any harm."

She smiled at Ben and Lily. "I'm sorry, kids. Joe is grumpy sometimes. He does not like people in his barn. But he does not mean to be mean. He loves his animals. He works hard to take care of them."

She pointed to the cow and the horse. "Do you want to meet them? They are friendly. They like to be petted. Their names are Daisy and Star."

Ben and Lily nodded. They wiped their tears and smiled. They walked to the animals and touched them gently. Daisy and Star nuzzled them and made soft noises.

"Thank you, ma'am," Ben said. "You are very nice. We like your animals. They are very nice too."

"Yes, thank you, ma'am," Lily said. "You are very kind. We are sorry for bothering you. We won't do it again."

Farmer Sue hugged them. "You are welcome, kids. You are very sweet. I'm glad you like our animals. You can come and visit them anytime. Just ask us first, okay?"

"Okay," Ben and Lily said.

They looked at Farmer Joe. He was still frowning, but he did not say anything. He looked at his wife and shrugged.

Ben and Lily said goodbye to Farmer Sue and the animals. They took their toy cars and ran back to their house. They were grateful for Farmer Sue. She was nice and kind. They were not grateful for Farmer Joe. He was mean and grumpy. They hoped he would be nicer next time. They decided to play with their toy cars on the grass. They liked to make noises and pretend they were racing. Sometimes they would pass each other and say "beep beep" or "vroom vroom".

"Wow, look at this!" Sara says. "This stamp is huge and pretty. I want it for myself."

"No, I want it for myself!" Ben says. "The lion is strong and brave. It is mine."

They both grab the stamp and pull hard. They do not want to share. They start to yell and cry.

Their mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the stamp and the twins. She is not happy.

"Stop it, Sara and Ben!" she says. "You are being selfish and rude. The stamp is not yours. It belongs to dad. He uses it for his work. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not fight over them. You should learn to share and be kind."

She takes the stamp and puts it back in the office. She hugs the twins and tells them to say sorry to each other. She also gives them some stickers and paper. They can make their own stamps with them.

Sara and Ben feel bad for what they did. They say sorry to each other and to their mom. They thank her for the stickers and paper. They start to make their own stamps with different shapes and colors. They have fun and share their stamps with each other. They learn that sharing is better than fighting.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the jungle. The jungle had many trees and animals and flowers. Lily and Ben liked to keep some flowers in their hair and some animals as their pets. They had a monkey, a bird, and a frog.

One day, they saw a big lion in the jungle. The lion was popular among the other animals. He was strong and brave and loud. Lily and Ben wanted to be friends with the lion, too. They thought he would like their flowers and pets.

They went to the lion and said, "Hello, lion. We are Lily and Ben. We like to play in the jungle. Do you want to play with us? We have flowers and pets for you."

The lion looked at them and smiled. He said, "Hello, Lily and Ben. I like to play in the jungle, too. And I like flowers and pets, too. But not in the way you think."

Lily and Ben did not understand what the lion meant. They gave him some flowers and showed him their pets. The lion took the flowers and ate them. He said, "Mmm, tasty flowers. Thank you."

Lily and Ben were surprised. They did not know that lions ate flowers. They said, "You're welcome, lion. But please don't eat our pets. They are our friends."

The lion laughed. He said, "Don't worry, Lily and Ben. I won't eat your pets. I will keep them. As my dinner."

Lily and Ben were scared. They realized that the lion was not a nice friend. He was a hungry enemy. They ran away from the lion as fast as they could. They hoped that their pets would escape, too.

The lion chased them and roared. He said, "Come back, Lily and Ben. I want to play with you. And eat you."

Lily and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned that not all animals in the jungle were friendly. And they learned that not all flowers and pets were safe. They decided to keep away from the lion and his popular friends. They decided to play with their own friends in a different part of the jungle.

Ben was a little boy who liked to play outside. One day, he saw a big tree with a hole in it. He wanted to see what was inside the hole. He put on his boots and his coat and went to the tree.

He crawled on the ground until he reached the tree. He looked up and saw the hole. It was dark and quiet. He wondered if there was an animal in there. He was not afraid. He was curious. He put his hand in the hole and felt something soft and warm.

Suddenly, he heard a loud hoot. He pulled his hand out and saw an owl. The owl had big eyes and a sharp beak. It looked angry. It flapped its wings and flew out of the hole. It landed on a branch and stared at Ben.

Ben was scared. He crawled away from the tree as fast as he could. He ran to his house and told his mom what he saw. His mom hugged him and said he was brave. She said the owl was probably protecting its babies. She said he should not bother the owl again.

Ben nodded. He learned his lesson. He was still curious, but he decided to leave the owl alone. He looked out the window and saw the owl sitting on the branch. It was raining and the owl was wet. Ben felt sorry for the owl. He hoped it would find a dry place to sleep. He said good night to the owl and went to bed.

Tom is a bald man who likes to gather rocks. He has many rocks of different colors and shapes in his house. He likes to show them to his friends and tell them where he found them.

One day, he goes to the park to look for more rocks. He sees a big rock that is shiny and smooth. He wants to take it home. He tries to lift it, but it is too heavy. He pulls and pulls, but it does not move. He feels a pain in his back. He says, "Ow, ow, ow!"

A little girl sees him and comes to help. She says, "Hello, mister. What are you doing?" Tom says, "I am trying to gather this rock, but it hurts my back. It is too heavy for me." The girl says, "Maybe you can use this." She gives him a stick. Tom says, "Thank you, little girl. What is your name?" The girl says, "I am Lily. I like rocks too. They are pretty and fun."

Tom uses the stick to roll the rock. He pushes and pushes, and the rock moves. He is happy. He says, "You are very smart, Lily. You helped me a lot. Do you want to see my other rocks?" Lily says, "Yes, please. I would love to see them." Tom says, "Come with me, then. I live nearby. We can be friends." Lily says, "Okay, mister. We can be friends. But you have to tell me your name too." Tom says, "I am Tom. I am a bald man who likes to gather rocks." Lily says, "I am Lily. I am a girl who likes to help." They smile and walk together, holding the stick and the rock.

"Help! Help!" he shouted. "The gum is on me!"

Lily heard him and ran to him. She saw the gum on his face and felt sorry. She tried to pull it off, but it was too sticky. She did not know what to do.

"Mom! Mom!" she called. "We need help!"

Their mom heard them and came to their room. She saw the mess and was angry. She scolded them for taking the gum and making trouble. She got some scissors and cut the gum off Max's face. She threw the gum in the trash and told them to clean their room.

Lily and Max felt bad and said sorry. They hugged each other and promised not to use gum for their show again. They learned their lesson and decided to perform something else.

Tom and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with cars and balls and books. They always shared their toys and helped each other.

One day, they went to the park with their moms. They saw a big slide and ran to it. They took turns to slide down and had a lot of fun. But then, Tom saw something shiny on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it. It was a passport. It had a picture of a man and some words he could not read.

"Look, Sam, I found a passport!" Tom said. "It is very pretty. I want to keep it."

Sam looked at the passport and shook his head. "No, Tom, you can't keep it. It is not yours. It belongs to someone else. Maybe they lost it and they are looking for it. We should give it to our moms. They can find the owner."

Tom frowned. He liked the passport. He wanted to have it. He put it in his pocket and said, "No, I found it. It is mine. You can't tell me what to do."

Sam was sad. He did not like how Tom was acting. He tried to talk to him, but Tom did not listen. He ran away from Sam and went to play with other kids.

Sam remained loyal to his friend. He hoped Tom would change his mind and do the right thing. He followed him and waited for a chance to talk to him again.

Soon, a man came to the park. He looked worried and sad. He asked the moms if they had seen his passport. He said he needed it to go back to his home. He said he had dropped it somewhere and he could not find it.

Sam heard the man and felt sorry for him. He knew where the passport was. He decided to tell the truth. He went to the man and said, "I know where your passport is. My friend Tom has it. He found it on the ground and he wanted to keep it. But I will get it for you. Please wait here."

Sam ran to Tom and said, "Tom, please give me the passport. The man who owns it is here. He needs it to go home. He is very sad. You should not keep something that is not yours. It is not nice. It is not fair."

Tom looked at Sam and then at the man. He saw how worried and sad the man was. He felt bad. He realized he was wrong. He took the passport out of his pocket and gave it to Sam. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. You are right. I should not have kept the passport. It was not mine. It was not nice. It was not fair. I'm sorry, man. Here is your passport. I hope you can go home soon."

Sam smiled and thanked Tom. He took the passport and gave it to the man. The man was very happy and grateful. He thanked Sam and Tom and hugged them. He said, "You are very good and brave boys. You did the right thing. You are very loyal to each other and to me. Thank you very much. You made my day."

Tom and Sam felt good. They learned a lesson. They learned to be honest and kind. They learned to respect other people's things. They learned to be loyal to their friends and to strangers. They hugged each other and went back to play. They remained best friends.

Tom hugs her and says, "It's OK, Jen. You tried your best. You are brave and strong. I will take you home and get you a band-aid. Maybe we can try again another day."

They walk back to their house. They watch the hill and wonder what is on the other side. They hope to find out someday. They are still friends.

"Only if the farmer says it's okay," mom said. "Some sheep might be dirty or scared of people."

They found the farmer and asked him. He smiled and said they could pet some of the sheep, but not the ones with red ribbons. Those were his prize sheep and he did not want them to get dirty.

Anna and Ben were happy and ran to the sheep. They saw one with a red ribbon and thought it was very pretty. It had long, curly wool and big, black eyes.

"Look, Ben, this one is so nice!" Anna said. "Let's wave to it and say hello."

They waved to the sheep and said hello. The sheep looked at them and baaed. Anna and Ben thought it wanted to be their friend. They went closer and tried to touch it.

But the sheep did not like that. It was angry and scared. It kicked Anna and Ben with its hooves and bit their hands. It made loud, angry noises and ran away.

Anna and Ben cried and ran to their mom. Their mom was very worried and angry. She saw their hands were bleeding and dirty. She took them to the farmer and told him what happened.

The farmer was very angry too. He said they were naughty and did not listen to him. He said they ruined his prize sheep and he wanted them to pay for it.

Mom had to give him a lot of money and say sorry. She took Anna and Ben to the car and drove them to the doctor. She said they were in big trouble and they could not go to the farm again.

Anna and Ben were very sad and sorry. They wished they had listened to mom and the farmer. They learned that some sheep are not nice and they should not wave to them.

Lily and Ben nodded, but they still looked at the sack with curious eyes. They wondered what Santa had wrapped for them. Maybe a doll for Lily and a truck for Ben. Or maybe something else. They wished they could peek inside.

They played with their toys for a while, but they soon got bored. They decided to sneak to the sack and touch it gently. Maybe they could feel what was inside.

They tiptoed to the sack and reached for it. But as soon as they touched it, they heard a loud snore. They jumped back and gasped. The sack was moving!

They looked at each other with wide eyes. Then they heard a voice from inside the sack.

"Ho ho ho! Merry Christmas, Lily and Ben! I'm sorry I fell asleep in your sack. I was so tired after delivering all the presents. I hope you don't mind if I stay here for a bit. You can open your presents later. But first, can you do me a favor and bring me some cookies and milk?"

Lily and Ben were shocked. Santa was in their sack! They couldn't believe it. They ran to Mommy and told her what they had seen and heard. Mommy laughed and hugged them.

"Of course, Santa is in our sack. He's our special guest. Let's go and give him some cookies and milk. And then we can open our presents together. What do you say?"

Lily and Ben nodded, excited. They grabbed some cookies and milk and followed Mommy to the sack. They saw Santa's red hat and beard sticking out of the sack. He smiled and winked at them.

"Thank you, Lily and Ben. You are very kind and good children. I have some wonderful presents for you. But first, let me wrap you in a big hug. Ho ho ho!"

Santa opened his arms and wrapped Lily and Ben in a warm hug. They giggled and hugged him back. They felt happy and loved. They couldn't wait to see what Santa had brought them. They knew it was going to be the best Christmas ever.

One day, he was feeling weak. He had a cold and his nose was runny. He did not want to play or eat. He just wanted to sleep. His mom came to his room and felt his forehead.

"Sam, you have a fever. You need to rest and drink some water," she said.

Sam did not like to rest. He wanted to guess. He looked at his mom and said, "Mom, can I guess something?"

"Sure, Sam. What do you want to guess?" his mom said.

Sam thought for a moment. He wanted to guess something hard, something that his mom would not know. He looked at the window and saw the sun shining.

"Mom, can I guess what day it is?" he asked.

His mom smiled. She knew what day it was, but she played along.

"Okay, Sam. What day do you think it is?" she asked.

Sam closed his eyes and tried to remember. He knew there were seven days in a week, but he always mixed them up. He opened his eyes and said, "Is it... Monday?"

His mom shook her head. "No, Sam. It's not Monday. It's Saturday. That's why you don't have to go to school today."

Sam frowned. He guessed wrong. He did not like to guess wrong. He wanted to guess right. He looked at his mom and said, "Mom, can I guess again?"

His mom nodded. "Sure, Sam. You can guess again. But first, you need to drink some water and take your medicine. Then you can guess as much as you want."

Sam agreed. He drank some water and took his medicine. He hoped they would make him feel better. He also hoped he would guess right the next time. He liked to guess, but he liked to guess right more.

He helped Spot out of the pit and gave him a small bone. He said, "Take this and go. And remember, be humble and grateful for what you have. There is enough for everyone if we are generous and kind."

Spot thanked the lion and ran away. He felt ashamed and grateful. He learned a valuable lesson that day. He decided to look for a new home and a new friend. He hoped to find someone who would love him and share with him. He never forgot the lion and his mercy. He always tried to be humble and kind.

From then on, Timmy knew he had to be careful around the cactus and not fight with the birds. He learned that sometimes things can be dangerous, but his mom would always be there to keep him safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys, especially her big teddy bear. One day, Lily was playing outside when she saw a large bird in the sky. The bird was so big that Lily could see it from far away.

Lily's mom came outside and saw the bird too. "That's a plane," said Lily's mom. "It's going to shoot a laser at the sky." Lily didn't know what a laser was, but she thought it sounded cool.

Later that day, Lily and her mom were walking to the park when they saw the same plane in the sky. Suddenly, a bright light shot out of the plane and into the clouds. "Wow!" said Lily. "That's the laser you told me about!"

Lily's mom smiled. "Yes, it is," she said. "But we should mind our heads and not look directly at the laser. It can hurt our eyes." Lily nodded and they continued walking to the park, excited to tell all their friends about the amazing plane and its laser.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring, and kindness is better than bullying.

"Come on, Mia, let's go up the hill!" Ben said.

"No, Ben, I want to pick flowers. They are pretty and smell good," Mia said.

"But the hill is fun and exciting. Maybe we can find a treasure or a cave," Ben said.

They argued for a while, but neither of them wanted to do what the other one wanted. They got angry and sad. Their mom and dad heard them and came to see what was wrong.

"Why are you fighting, Ben and Mia?" their mom asked.

"Ben wants to climb the hill and I want to pick flowers," Mia said.

"Mia wants to pick flowers and I want to climb the hill," Ben said.

Their dad looked at the hill and saw that it was very steep and deep. He saw some loose rocks and holes that could be dangerous.

"Ben, I don't think it's a good idea to climb the hill. It's too deep and you could get hurt. Why don't you pick some flowers with Mia instead? They are beautiful and you can make a bouquet for mom," he said.

"But dad, I want to see what's on the hill. Maybe there's something cool up there," Ben said.

"Mia, why don't you try to climb the hill with Ben? Maybe you can see something new and learn something. It's good to explore and be curious," their mom said.

"But mom, I don't like the hill. It's too high and scary. I like the flowers better. They are soft and nice," Mia said.

"Ben and Mia, we love you both very much. We want you to have fun and be happy at camp. But we also want you to be safe and kind. And sometimes, you have to do things that make others happy, even if they are not your favorite things. That's how you show love and care. Why don't you try to do both? You can pick some flowers and then climb the hill together. Or you can climb the hill and then pick some flowers together. What do you think?" they said.

Ben and Mia thought about it and nodded. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to pick some flowers and then climb the hill together. They had fun and saw many things. Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play with words. They had a big book with many words and what they meant. They called it a dictionary. They liked to learn new words and use them in their games.

One day, Tom came to Lily's house with his dictionary. He wanted to show her a word he had learned. But when he opened his bag, the dictionary was not there. He felt sad and angry. He said, "Where is my dictionary? I need it for our game. Did you take it, Lily?"

Lily was surprised and hurt. She said, "No, Tom, I did not take your dictionary. Why would I do that? I have my own dictionary. Maybe you left it at home or at school."

Tom did not believe her. He said, "You are lying, Lily. You are jealous of my dictionary. You wanted to have it for yourself. You are a bad friend."

Lily started to cry. She said, "No, Tom, you are wrong. I am not jealous. I am not lying. I am your friend. But you are being mean to me. You are hurting my feelings."

Tom and Lily stopped playing and went to their own houses. They did not talk to each other for a long time. They missed each other, but they were too proud to say sorry.

One day, Tom's mom found his dictionary under his bed. It was hidden by his toys. She said, "Tom, look what I found. It is your dictionary. You must have forgotten it here. Do you remember who you wanted to show it to?"

Tom remembered Lily. He felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "Mom, I wanted to show it to Lily. But I thought she took it from me. I was rude to her. I made her cry. I was a bad friend."

Tom's mom said, "Tom, you made a mistake. You should not accuse your friend without proof. You should trust your friend and be kind to her. You should apologize to her and make up with her. Do you want to do that?"

Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, mom, I want to do that. I want to be a good friend. I want to play with Lily again. I miss her."

Tom's mom said, "That's good, Tom. I am proud of you. Let's go to Lily's house and bring her your dictionary. Maybe you can teach her the new word you learned."

Tom and Lily were happy to see each other. They hugged and said sorry. They looked at the dictionary and learned the new word. They played with words and had fun. They were friends again.

The moral of the story is: Don't jump to conclusions and accuse your friends. Trust your friends and be kind to them. Say sorry when you make a mistake. Friendship is more important than things.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play all day. She had many toys and books and games, but she never wanted to stop and rest. She always said, "I am not tired, I want to play more!"

One night, Lily was playing with her doll and her lamp. She liked to turn the lamp on and off and make shadows on the wall. She did not listen when her mom told her to go to bed. She said, "I am not sleepy, I want to play more!"

But soon, Lily felt her eyes get heavy and her head get dizzy. She was too tired to play, but she did not want to admit it. She tried to keep her eyes open, but they closed by themselves. She fell asleep on the floor, with her doll and her lamp.

The next morning, Lily woke up with a sore neck and a bad mood. She did not want to get up or eat or talk. She felt grumpy and sad. Her mom saw her and said, "Lily, you did not rest enough last night. You played too much with your lamp and you did not sleep in your bed. That is why you feel bad today. You need to rest your body and your mind, or you will not be happy or healthy."

Lily realized that her mom was right. She had been too stubborn and selfish. She had not thought about how her lamp needed to rest too, or how her mom wanted her to be safe and comfortable. She said, "I am sorry, mom. You are right. I need to rest more and play less. I will not play with my lamp at night anymore. I will sleep in my bed and turn off the lamp. I will be a good girl and listen to you."

Lily hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. Thank you for taking care of me." Her mom hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's have some breakfast and start a new day."

The moral of the story is: Rest is important for your body and your mind. You should not play too much or too late, or you will feel tired and unhappy. You should listen to your parents and follow their rules, because they want what is best for you. You should be grateful for what you have and take care of it, because it might not last forever.

After they found the toy car, Lily's mom told her how proud she was of her for being so kind and helpful. Lily felt calm and happy inside. She learned that helping others can make a big difference and make people feel better. From that day on, Lily always tried to help others whenever she could.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max who loved to surf. He would ride the waves all day long, but he always made sure to return home before dinner time.

One day, Max met a new friend at the beach. His friend was a seagull named Sammy. They talked about the waves and how much fun they were having. Max was happy to have a loyal friend like Sammy.

As the sun began to set, Max realized it was time to go home. He said goodbye to Sammy and promised to return the next day for more surfing fun.

The next day, Max was excited to surf with Sammy again. But when he arrived at the beach, Sammy was nowhere to be found. Max searched and searched, but his friend was gone.

Feeling sad and alone, Max continued to surf. Suddenly, he saw a familiar bird flying towards him. It was Sammy! He had returned to surf with Max again.

From that day on, Max and Sammy surfed together every day. They were loyal friends who always returned to the beach for more fun in the waves.

Timmy said, "Don't be scared, Lily. We can learn about dragons in books. Let's go to the library and find a book about dragons."

So, they went to the library and found a book about dragons. They learned that dragons are not scary and they can be friendly too. From that day on, Lily and Timmy were not scared of dragons anymore. They even made a new friend who was a dragon!

Once upon a time, there was a wild cat named Tom. One day, Tom saw a little mouse named Jerry. Tom wanted to catch Jerry and eat him up. So, Tom started to crawl towards Jerry.

Jerry saw Tom coming towards him and got scared. Jerry asked, "Why are you coming towards me, Tom?" Tom replied, "I want to catch you and eat you up."

Jerry had an idea. He said, "Hey Tom, do you see that triangle over there? Let's go and play there instead of fighting." Tom thought it was a good idea and they both went to play at the triangle. From that day on, Tom and Jerry became friends and never fought again.

As it was taking a bath, it saw something blink in the water. It was a shiny object that looked like a necklace. The ostrich picked it up and put it around its neck.

The other animals in the field were amazed at how clean and shiny the ostrich looked with its new necklace. From that day on, the ostrich made sure to keep its feathers clean and shiny, and it always wore its special necklace.

Just then, a boy came running towards the girl. He had been playing nearby and saw the girl in trouble. The boy had a rope in his hand, so he used it to grab the frog. Then he took the frog far away and put it back in the pond.

The girl thanked the boy for helping her and asked why he was so brave. The boy said it was because he was not stupid and wanted to be her friend. 

The girl was very happy and hugged the boy for rescuing her from the frog. The boy smiled, and they both laughed and decided to play together with the rope.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lily. Lily was three years old and she loved presents.

One afternoon, Lily was in her bedroom playing with her toys when she heard a loud noise. It was a very loud scream. Lily was scared, so she called for her mommy. 

Her mommy came into the room and asked her what was the matter. Lily told her mommy she had heard a loud scream. Her mommy said that there were no monsters in her bedroom, but Lily still felt scared.

Then, suddenly, Lily noticed something. It was a present, sitting in the corner of the room. It was wrapped in shiny wrapping paper and a big bow.

Lily was very excited! She looked at her mommy with charming eyes and said, "Can I open it?" Her mommy said yes, so Lily opened the present.

When she opened it, Lily saw something which made her scream with joy - it was a brand new doll! All of Lily's fear disappeared and she was so happy that she wanted to give her mommy a big hug.

Lily played with her new doll all day long. She couldn't believe how lucky she was to have such a charming present.

Once upon a time there was a small girl, who was very confused. She had just sneezed and could not understand why.

The girl looked around her, and her eyes fell on the rug. She had never noticed it there before. The rug was very soft and colourful, with green, blue and yellow stripes.

The girl stepped onto the rug and immediately sneezed again. She wondered why it was making her sneeze. So she decided to lie down on the rug and wait.

After a few minutes, the girl heard a noise. It sounded like a whisper. She looked around, but all she saw was the rug.

When she touched the rug, the whisper became louder. "Sneeze again, and I'll tell you why you're sneezing." The girl got confused, but then she sneezed again.

Suddenly, the rug spoke. "Your sneezing is because I'm tickling your nose!" The girl laughed, then sneezed again, and the rug laughed too.

And ever since then, the girl and the rug would play together, whenever she sneezed.

One day Bob decided to take his trumpet and find a place he'd never been before. He went over hills and through dales until he spotted something special - a circus!

The circus looked amazing, but Bob was too scared to go in. Still, the loud music of the trumpets excited him and so he decided to go in for a closer look.

The clowns were jumping and the acrobats were spinning. Soon, Bob spotted a friendly clown and he asked if he could have a go on the trumpet.

The clown handed it to him and Bob blew into it. He was so excited that he'd made a noise on the trumpet that he raced around the circus, making laughter and smiles with every trumpet sound.

Bob was so happy that he kept playing long after the circus had gone. The jolly trumpet sounds filled the air and Bob smiled from ear to ear.

Back inside, they decided to play chess again. Jack and Lily tried their hardest to think of clever moves. Jack was very patient and Lily was good at playing, so it was an enjoyable game for both of them. 

At the end of the day, Jack and Lily were both tired but happy. They said goodbye and promised to listen, play chess and be patient with each other always.

The next day, Sara and her mom went to the park. Sara saw many trees, flowers, and animals. She ran and played and had fun. She saw the same bird from her window. It was sitting on a branch, singing. Sara was happy to see it again.

She ran towards the bird, hoping to make friends. But the bird was scared and flew away. Sara was sad and stopped. She heard a loud noise behind her. She turned and saw a big truck. It was coming fast and did not see her.

Her mom saw the truck and ran to Sara. She grabbed her and pulled her away. They fell on the grass, safe. Sara was scared and cried. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Sara. You're okay. I'm here."

Sara looked at her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. You saved me." She looked at the sky and saw the bird. It was flying high and free. She said, "Bye, bird. Be careful." She hoped the bird would be okay too.

"Wow, look at the jet!" Tom says. "I want to fly in a jet one day."

"Me too," Mia says. "Let's pretend we are jets and zoom around the park."

They run and jump and make jet noises. They have fun. But they are careless. They do not look where they are going. They do not see the pond.

Splash! Tom and Mia fall into the water. They are wet and cold and scared. They cry for help.

"Help! Help!" they shout.

A man hears them and comes to the pond. He pulls them out of the water. He is angry.

"What are you doing here?" he asks. "This pond is dangerous. You could have drowned. You are very careless. Where are your parents?"

Tom and Mia do not know. They ran away from their parents when they saw the jet. They are sorry. They are in trouble.

The man takes them to their parents. Their parents are worried and mad. They scold them and take them home. They do not let them play in the park for a long time.

Tom and Mia are sad. They wish they were not careless. They wish they did not see the jet. They wish they did not pretend to be jets. They wish they just gathered rocks and sticks and made houses for their toys.

Ben felt sad. He did not like when Sara was mean. He said, "It is not nice to say that. Humble means you are not proud or rude. You are rude, Sara. You should share your toys."

Sara did not listen. She kept making her castle. She said, "I do not want to share. These are my toys. You can play with your humble toy."

Ben looked around. He saw a towel on the grass. It was blue and soft. He had an idea. He said, "Can I use your towel, Sara?"

Sara said, "Why do you want my towel? It is not a toy. It is for drying."

Sara nodded. She said, "Yes, Ben. I want to play with it. Can we play together?"

Sara smiled too. She said, "That sounds fun, Ben. I am sorry I was rude. You are not humble. You are clever and kind."

They started to tug and pull on the flashlight, each trying to get it from the other. They did not see the rock on the ground behind them. Tom stumbled and fell, and the flashlight flew out of his hand. It landed on the rock and broke. The light went out and the glass cracked.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried, rubbing his knee. He had scraped it on the rock and it hurt. He looked at the flashlight and saw that it was broken. He felt sad and angry. He blamed Mia for making him fall.

"That's your fault, Mia!" he shouted. "You broke the flashlight! You are mean and bad!"

He got up and kicked the flashlight hard. It flew in the air and hit Mia on the head. She gasped and dropped to the ground. She felt a bump on her head and it hurt. She looked at Tom and saw that he was mad. She felt scared and sorry. She did not mean to break the flashlight.

"I'm sorry, Tom!" she cried. "I didn't mean to break the flashlight! I just wanted to play with it! Please don't be mad at me!"

She reached out her hand to Tom, hoping he would forgive her. Tom looked at her hand and then at her face. He saw that she was hurt and sad. He felt bad for kicking the flashlight and hitting her. He did not want to be mean and bad.

"I'm sorry, Mia!" he said. "I didn't mean to kick the flashlight and hit you! I was just mad and sad! Please don't be scared of me!"

He took her hand and helped her up. They hugged and said they were sorry again. They decided to share the flashlight and play with it together. They went inside and showed their mom the flashlight. Anna and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But they did not like the grumpy man who lived near the park. He always shouted at them and told them to go away.

One day, Anna and Ben saw a big tree in the park. It had many leaves and branches. They wanted to climb the tree and see the birds and the sky. But the grumpy man saw them and came out of his house. He said, "Get off my tree! It is mine! You are bad children!"

Anna and Ben were scared and sad. They did not want to make the grumpy man angry. They got off the tree and ran away. But the grumpy man was not happy. He wanted to cut the tree and make it small. He got a big saw and went to the tree.

Anna and Ben saw the grumpy man with the saw. They felt sorry for the tree. They wanted to save the tree and the birds. They had an idea. They found a big stick and a big stone. They ran back to the park and hid behind a bush.

When the grumpy man was about to saw the tree, Anna and Ben jumped out of the bush. They shouted, "Stop! Leave the tree alone!" They threw the stone at the saw and made it fall. Then they pushed the grumpy man with the stick and made him fall too.

The grumpy man was surprised and angry. He said, "You little brats! How dare you!" He tried to get up and chase them. But the tree was happy and grateful. It moved its branches and wrapped them around the grumpy man. It said, "Thank you, Anna and Ben. You are good children. You are my friends."

Anna and Ben smiled and hugged the tree. They said, "You are welcome, tree. You are our friend too. We are sorry for the grumpy man. He is mean and lonely. Maybe he needs a hug too."

The tree thought for a moment. Then it loosened its branches and let the grumpy man go. It said, "Maybe you are right, Anna and Ben. Maybe he needs a hug too. Here, grumpy man, have a hug from me."

The grumpy man was shocked and confused. He felt the tree's branches around him. He felt the tree's warmth and kindness. He felt something he had not felt for a long time. He felt happy.

He said, "Thank you, tree. You are not so bad. You are a nice tree. And thank you, Anna and Ben. You are not so bad either. You are brave and smart. Maybe we can be friends too."

Anna and Ben nodded and smiled. They said, "Yes, we can be friends too. We can play in the park and share the tree. We can have fun and be happy."

And that is what they did. They played in the park and shared the tree. They had fun and were happy. And the grumpy man was not so grumpy anymore. He was a friend.

"Let's surprise Dad when he comes back from the field," Tom said. "We can roll the barrel to the door and jump out when he opens it."

"OK, but we have to be quiet and strong," Sam said. "The barrel is heavy and Dad is smart. He might hear us or see us."

They waited inside the barrel for a long time. They heard the cows moo and the birds sing. They heard the tractor stop and the door open. They got ready to surprise Dad.

But it was not Dad who opened the door. It was a big dog who smelled the barrel and barked. The dog pushed the barrel with his nose and made it roll. Tom and Sam screamed and held on tight. The barrel rolled out of the barn and down the hill. It bumped into rocks and trees and went faster and faster.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Sam shouted. "We want to stop!"

Dad heard their cries and ran after them. He was strong and fast. He caught up with the barrel and stopped it with his hands. He opened the lid and saw his sons. They were scared and dirty and sorry.

"What were you doing in there?" Dad asked. "Are you OK?"

"We wanted to surprise you, but we surprised ourselves," Tom said.

"We're sorry, Dad. We won't do it again," Sam said.

Dad hugged them and smiled. He was not angry. He was glad they were safe.

"Next time, surprise me with a hug or a drawing, not a barrel," he said. "Now let's go home and clean up."

Mom and dad hugged Lily and Sam. They wiped their tears and water. They gave them their hat and bag. They said they were sorry. They said they would fix the jeep and go back to the camp. They said they loved them.

Lily and Sam felt better. They said they loved them too. They said they still liked the safari. But they did not like the monkey. They said the monkey was bad and naughty. Mom and dad agreed. They said the monkey was bad and naughty. But they also said the monkey was funny. They all laughed.

Sam and Ben are friends who like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They pretend to drive them on the road, in the park, and in the garage. They make sounds like vroom, beep, and screech.

One day, Sam finds a new car in his toy box. It is shiny and red, and it has a gear that can make it go faster or slower. Sam is very happy and shows it to Ben. Ben likes the new car too, and asks Sam if he can play with it.

"Sorry, Ben, this is my car. You can play with your regular cars. They are still good," Sam says.

"But I want to try the new car. Please, Sam, can I have a turn?" Ben begs.

"No, Ben, this is my car. Go away," Sam says. He drives the new car away from Ben, and parks it in a corner.

Ben is sad and angry. He thinks Sam is not a good friend. He looks around and sees a big ball. He has an idea. He kicks the ball hard, and it flies towards Sam's new car. It hits the car and knocks it over. The car breaks and the gear falls out.

Sam hears the noise and sees his new car broken. He is very sad and angry. He runs to Ben and shouts, "Why did you do that, Ben? You broke my new car. You are a bad friend."

Ben says, "You are a bad friend too, Sam. You did not share your new car with me. You were mean and selfish."

Sam and Ben start to cry. They do not want to play with each other anymore. They sit apart and hold their toys.

A grown-up sees them and comes to talk to them. She says, "What happened, Sam and Ben? Why are you crying?"

Sam and Ben tell her what happened. They blame each other for breaking the car and not sharing.

The grown-up says, "I'm sorry that your car is broken, Sam. But you should have shared it with Ben. He is your friend, and friends share their toys. Sharing makes everyone happy. And Ben, you should not have kicked the ball at Sam's car. That was not nice. You should have asked him nicely, or played with something else. Kicking makes everyone sad."

Sam and Ben listen to the grown-up. They feel sorry for what they did. They say sorry to each other, and hug. They decide to share their toys, and play together again. They fix the car with some tape, and take turns to drive it. They also play with the ball, and the regular cars. They have fun, and laugh.

The grown-up smiles and says, "That's better, Sam and Ben. You are good friends now. Remember, sharing and being kind are better than being mean and selfish. That is the moral of this story."

Lily was embarrassed. She did not mean to do anything bad. She just wanted to see Max. She got down from the chair and said sorry to Mom.

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I know you love Max, but he is very fragile. You have to be gentle and careful with him. You can look at him and talk to him, but only when I am with you. OK?"

"Mom, can we have some vegetables?" Lily called.

"Yes, you can, but only one each. And you have to catch them first!" Mom said. She smiled and threw a carrot in the air.

Lily and Tom ran to catch the carrot. They both reached for it, but it fell to the ground. Mom threw another carrot, and then a tomato, and then a cucumber. Lily and Tom tried to catch them, but they were too fast or too high or too slippery.

"Mom, this is hard!" Tom said.

"Mom, this is fun!" Lily said.

Mom threw one last vegetable. It was a big, round, green cabbage. Lily and Tom both wanted it. They ran towards it, but they bumped into each other and fell down. The cabbage rolled away.

"Oh no!" Lily and Tom said.

They got up and chased the cabbage. It rolled down the hill, past the flowers, past the fence, past the dog. Lily and Tom ran after it, but they could not catch it. The cabbage rolled into the road, where a big truck was coming.

"Stop!" Mom shouted.

Lily and Tom stopped. They saw the truck hit the cabbage and smash it into pieces. They were scared and sad.

"Mom, we're sorry!" Lily and Tom said.

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay, my loves. I'm glad you're safe. You don't have to catch vegetables to eat them. You just have to be clever and share them. Come on, let's go back to the basket and pick one each. And remember, always look both ways before you cross the road."

Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We love you."

They went back to the basket and picked one vegetable each. They ate them happily and thanked Mom for the fun game. They learned to be clever and share and be careful. They had a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Pinchy who lived in a big ocean. Pinchy loved to play on the shore, where the sand was warm and the waves tickled his claws. 

One day, Pinchy saw a big wave coming towards the shore. He knew it was going to be a big one because the water was moving fast. Pinchy scurried back towards the ocean, but he wasn't fast enough. The wave crashed onto the shore and swept Pinchy into the water. 

Pinchy was scared because he didn't know how to swim very well. He tried to paddle his little legs, but he couldn't keep his head above the water. Just when he thought he was going to be swept away, a friendly dolphin came to his rescue. The dolphin helped Pinchy back to the shore, where he could feel the warm sand beneath his claws once again. From that day on, Pinchy was always careful when he played on the shore.

Bow was very happy to win the prize. He took the big, yummy bone home with him. Bow shared the bone with his friends. They all had a great time. Bow was not impatient anymore, because he learned that good things come when you wait.

Once upon a time, in a small classroom, there was a noisy group of kids. They liked to play and talk a lot. The sun would shine through the window and make the room bright and warm.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to show his friends a shiny toy. He said, "Look at my shiny toy! It is so pretty!" But the other kids were too noisy and did not hear him. Tim felt sad.

Tim tried again and again to show his shiny toy to his friends. But they were always noisy and never listened. In the end, Tim's shiny toy got lost, and he never found it again.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain. A long, long time ago, a cat and a dog lived on this mountain. The cat and dog were friends. They liked to play together. One day, they found a big ball.

The cat and the dog wanted to play with the ball. The cat wanted to spin the ball, but the dog wanted to roll the ball. They could not agree. The cat said, "I want to spin the ball." The dog said, "No, I want to roll the ball."

The cat and the dog were sad. They did not want to fight. They wanted to play together. Then, they had an idea. They decided to take turns. First, the cat would spin the ball. Then, the dog would roll the ball.

The cat and the dog played with the ball for a long, long time. They were happy. They learned that they could play together if they shared. And they stayed friends on the big mountain forever.

Once upon a time, in a big green field, there was a small rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to play and hop all day long. One day, Remy saw a big tree with a small hole close to its bottom. He thought it would be fun to look inside.

As Remy hopped closer to the tree, he felt cold air coming from the hole. He thought, "I wonder what is making the air so cold?" Remy was very curious and wanted to find out. So, he put his little paw inside the hole and felt something soft and cold.

Remy pulled the cold thing out of the hole. It was a big, cold, shiny rock! He showed it to his rabbit friends and they all thought it was very special. They decided to keep the cold rock close to them, so they put it in a safe place near their rabbit homes.

As the days went by, Remy and his friends noticed that the cold rock made their homes feel nice and cool on hot days. They were so happy to have found the cold rock and kept it close to them always. And that is how Remy and his friends stayed cool and happy all summer long.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn little boy named Tim. Tim had a favorite shoe that he loved very much. He would wear it every day and never wanted to take it off.

One day, Tim's mom told him, "Tim, it's time to wear your new shoes. Your old shoe is dirty and has a hole." But Tim did not want to wear his new shoes. He said, "No, Mom! I want my old shoe."

Tim's mom tried to take the old shoe off, but Tim slapped her hand away. His mom was sad, but she did not give up. She said, "Tim, if you wear your new shoes, we can go to the park and play."

Tim thought about it and finally agreed. He put on his new shoes and went to the park with his mom. At the park, Tim had so much fun that he forgot all about his old shoe. From that day on, Tim was not stubborn about his shoes anymore.

But then, Lily came and saw the dirty scarf. She said, "Don't worry, Spot. We can wash the scarf and it will be clean again." Spot was happy and they both cleaned the scarf together.

Sally told Carl, "I recommend you try to slow down and be more careful when you move." Carl listened to Sally and tried to be more careful. But he was still very clumsy. Carl was sad and worried that he would always be like this.

One day, Carl saw a big, pretty butterfly flying in the sky. He wanted to be like the butterfly and fly too. He thought that if he could fly, he would not be clumsy anymore. He tried to climb a tall flower to get closer to the sky. But as he climbed, he slipped and fell down. Carl was hurt and could not move anymore. He wished he had listened to Sally's advice and been more careful.

They saw a bird lying on the ground. The bird was not moving. The cat said, "Oh no, the bird is dead." They felt sad for the bird. The dog said, "Let's be more careful with the glue." They agreed and played safely from then on.

But Lily refused. She was too bossy and proud. She said she did not need their help. She said she only needed her doll. She said no to her friends.

That was a big mistake. The dog did not give up. It bit the doll and tore it apart. Lily watched in horror as her doll became zero. She had nothing left. She was alone and sad.

She wished she had listened to her mom and shared her toys. She wished she had been nice to her friends and played with them. She wished she had said yes instead of no.

But it was too late. She had learned her lesson the hard way. She had lost her doll and her friends. She had been too bossy and refused.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and listen to music. One day, they find a radio in the garage. The radio is old and broken. It does not make any sound.

"Can we fix it?" Anna asks.

"Maybe," Ben says. "We need to find the part that is missing."

They look around the garage. They see many things: a ball, a bike, a hammer, a screwdriver, a box, a can, a rope, a hat. But they do not see the part.

"Where is it?" Anna wonders.

"Let's ask Dad," Ben suggests.

They go to the house and find Dad. He is reading a book.

"Dad, can you help us?" Ben says.

"What do you need, son?" Dad asks.

"We want to fix the radio. But we can't find the part," Ben explains.

Dad smiles. He puts down his book and follows them to the garage. He looks at the radio.

"This is a very old radio," he says. "It needs a battery to work. Do you know what a battery is?"

Anna and Ben shake their heads.

"A battery is a thing that has power. It makes the radio play music. But this battery is empty. It has no power. We need a new battery," Dad says.

"Where can we get a new battery?" Anna asks.

"We can buy one at the store. Or we can use one from another toy. Do you have a toy that has a battery?" Dad asks.

Anna and Ben think. They remember that they have a toy car that has a battery. They run to their room and get the toy car.

"Here it is!" Ben says.

"Good job!" Dad says. "You are very clever. You can use this battery for the radio. Let me show you how."

Dad opens the toy car and takes out the battery. He opens the radio and puts in the battery. He turns on the radio. It makes a sound.

"It works!" Anna and Ben cheer.

They hear music and voices. They dance and sing. They are happy.

"Thank you, Dad!" they say.

"You're welcome, kids," Dad says. "You learned something today. You learned that some things need power to work. And you learned that you can use one thing for another thing. That is called recycling. Recycling is good. It helps us save money and the earth. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nod.

"Yes, Dad," they say. "We understand. Recycling is good. And we are clever."

Dad hugs them.

"Yes, you are," he says. "And I am proud of you."

One day, she found a new car in her toy box. It was shiny and red, with black stripes and a big spoiler. It looked very fast and cool. Jenny did not know where it came from. Maybe her mom or dad gave it to her as a surprise. She decided to call it Blaze.

Jenny felt better and calmed down. She understood that the car was not unknown, but a model. She understood that the car was not dangerous, but fun. She understood that the car was not a spy, but a friend. She decided to give the car another chance and play with it again.

"Let go of it!" Tom shouted. "It is mine!"

"Never!" Sam shouted back. "It is mine!"

They kept pulling and shouting, until they heard a loud hiss. They looked up and saw a snake on the tree. It was angry and hungry. It had been sleeping on the mushroom, and did not like to be disturbed.

The snake opened its mouth and bit Tom on the arm. Tom screamed and let go of the mushroom. He fell to the ground and felt very sick. Sam saw the snake and ran away. He was scared and sorry. He did not want to own the mushroom anymore.

The snake curled up on the mushroom and went back to sleep. It was happy and full. It did not care who owned the mushroom. It only cared about itself.
