"Hey, this is my rock!" Ben exclaimed, angry. "You took it from me!"

"No, I didn't!" Anna protested, trying to grab it back. "I found it first!"

They started to tug and pull on the rock, each wanting to have it. They did not see their mom coming out of the house.

"Kids, what are you doing?" Mom asked, surprised. "Why are you fighting over a rock?"

They stopped and looked at Mom, ashamed. They knew they had done something wrong.

"We're sorry, Mom," they said in unison.

Mom smiled and hugged them. "It's okay, I know you both like shiny things. But you have to share and be nice to each other. How about we go inside and make some cookies? Maybe we can find some chocolate chips that are shiny too."

Anna and Ben nodded and smiled. They forgot about the rock and followed Mom inside. They decided they liked cookies more than rocks. And they liked playing together more than fighting. They were happy and not envious anymore.

But then, she hears a loud noise. It is her baby brother, who is in his crib. He is crying and making a fuss. He wants to wake up and play. Sara puts down her crayon and runs to his room. She sees him kicking his blanket and waving his arms. She wants to make him feel better.

Her brother stops crying and looks at her drawing. He smiles and reaches for it. He likes the colors and the shapes. He grabs the paper and tears it. He laughs and claps his hands. He thinks it is fun.

Sara is sad and angry. She worked hard on her drawing and now it is ruined. She says, "No, no, no! That is my drawing! You can't tear it! You are a bad brother!" She snatches the paper and the crayon from him. She starts to cry.

Her mom hugs her and says, "I'm sorry, Sara. I know you are upset. But your brother is not a bad brother. He is just a baby. He doesn't know how to draw or how to be careful. Sara feels a little better. She says, "Okay, mom. I forgive him. He is a baby. He doesn't know. I love him and I want to be a good sister. Can I give him another toy and play with him?"

Her mom says, "Yes, Sara. That is very nice of you. You can give him another toy and play with him. But please, no more sharp crayons. They are not for you. They are for grown-ups. Use your other crayons. They are safer and prettier. And maybe you can make another drawing for me. I would love to see it."

Sara says, "Okay, mom. I will use my other crayons. And I will make another drawing for you. Thank you, mom. I love you."

Her mom says, "I love you too, Sara. And I love your brother. You are both my precious children. Now, let's play together and have some fun."

One day, a hunter went to the forest to look for animals. He saw a big bear sleeping under a tree. He wanted to catch the bear and take it home. He took out his net and tried to throw it over the bear.

But the bear woke up and saw the hunter. The bear was very angry and roared loudly. The hunter was frightened and ran away. He dropped his net and his hat on the ground.

The bear followed the hunter and saw a house. The house was made of wood and straw. The hunter had built it himself. The bear thought it was a good place to hide. He pushed the door and went inside.

The hunter ran back to his house. He wanted to get his gun and shoot the bear. He opened the door and saw the bear sitting on his bed. The hunter was very surprised and scared. He said, "Please, don't hurt me! This is my house!"

The bear looked at the hunter and said, "This is your house? You built it yourself? Why did you try to catch me? I was sleeping peacefully in the forest. You should not bother the animals. They have their own homes too."

The hunter felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "You are right. I was wrong. I should not have tried to catch you. I am sorry. Please, forgive me. You can stay in my house if you want."

The bear smiled and said, "Thank you. You are very kind. I forgive you. But I don't want to stay in your house. I want to go back to the forest. That is my home. Goodbye, hunter. And remember, be nice to the animals."

The hunter nodded and said, "Goodbye, bear. And thank you. I will remember. Be nice to the animals."

The bear left the house and went back to the forest. The hunter learned a lesson. He never tried to catch the animals again. He lived happily in his house. He and the bear became friends.

The end.

Moral value: We should respect the animals and their homes. We should not harm them or take them away from their natural habitats. We should be kind and friendly to all living beings.

"Be careful, Jen. The mixer is very powerful. You have to use it with adult supervision," Mr. Lee said. He plugged the mixer into the wall and turned it on. The mixer made a loud noise and spun very fast.

"Can we try it, Mr. Lee?" Sam asked.

"Okay, but only for a little bit. And don't put your fingers near the blades. They are very sharp," Mr. Lee said. He gave them a bowl and some ingredients and showed them how to use the mixer.

Jen and Sam were very happy. They poured the eggs, flour, sugar, and butter into the bowl and turned on the mixer. The batter looked yummy and smooth.

"Can we add some chocolate chips?" Jen asked.

"Sure, why not?" Mr. Lee said. He gave them a bag of chocolate chips and told them to sprinkle some on top of the batter.

Jen and Sam did as he said. They opened the bag and poured some chocolate chips into the bowl. But they poured too much. The bowl was full of chocolate chips and the mixer could not mix them.

The mixer started to make a strange noise. It sounded like it was angry. It shook and rattled and smoked. Jen and Sam were scared. They tried to turn off the mixer, but they could not. The mixer was too strong.

"Help, Mr. Lee! The mixer is broken!" Jen cried.

Mr. Lee heard them and ran to the kitchen. He saw the mixer going crazy and the batter flying everywhere. He tried to unplug the mixer, but he was too late. The mixer exploded with a loud bang. The kitchen was a mess. There was batter and chocolate chips and metal pieces all over the floor, the walls, the ceiling, and the people.

Jen and Sam and Mr. Lee were covered in sticky goo. They looked at each other and felt very sad. They had ruined the mixer and the cake and the kitchen.

"Sorry, Mr. Lee. We did not mean to break your mixer," Sam said.

"It's okay, Sam. It was an accident. But you should have been more careful. The mixer was very expensive and hard to replace," Mr. Lee said.

"What about the cake for Jen's mom?" Jen asked.

"I'm afraid there is no cake for Jen's mom. We have to clean up this mess and buy a new mixer and start over," Mr. Lee said.

Jen and Sam felt very bad. They had wanted to make a cake for Jen's mom, but they had made a big mistake. They had not listened to Mr. Lee and they had used the mixer without adult supervision. They had learned a hard lesson. They wished they had never borrowed the mixer. They wished they had never met Mr. Lee. They wished they had never been born. The end.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill with snow on it. They wanted to slide down the hill on their sleds. They ran to the hill with their sleds and took turns sliding down.

Tim had a red sled that was fast and shiny. Sam had a blue sled that was old and dull. Tim liked his sled more than Sam's sled. He thought his sled was better and more fun. He did not want to share his sled with Sam.

Sam asked Tim if he could try his red sled. Tim said no. He said his sled was only for him. Sam felt sad and hurt. He did not understand why Tim did not want to share. He thought they were friends.

Sam went back to his blue sled and slid down the hill. He tried to have fun, but he missed Tim. He wished they could play together.

But then, something bad happened. Tim hit a bump on the hill and flew off his sled. He landed on the icy ground and hurt his arm. He cried out in pain and fear. He looked around for help, but he saw no one. He was alone.

Sam heard Tim's cry and looked up. He saw Tim on the ground, holding his arm. He felt sorry for Tim and worried about him. He forgot about the sleds and ran to Tim. He helped him get up and hugged him. He said he was sorry and asked if he was okay.

Tim felt Sam's hug and heard his words. He felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he had been mean and selfish. He had not been a good friend. He said he was sorry and thanked Sam. He asked if he could share his red sled with him.

Sam smiled and nodded. He said he would love to share his sled with him. He said they were friends and friends share. He said he was glad Tim was okay.

They hugged again and went back to the hill. They took turns sliding down on the red sled and the blue sled. They had fun and laughed. They learned to accept each other and their sleds. They learned to be kind and generous. They learned to be true friends.

"No, Ben! Stop!" Sara said. She picked up her bunny and hugged it. "You are mean! You make my bunny scared!"

"I don't care! Your bunny is ugly!" Ben said. He grabbed Sara's bunny and threw it on the floor.

Sara started to cry. She ran to her mom and told her what Ben did. Mom was angry. She went to the hall and saw Ben's truck.

"Ben, come here!" Mom said. "Why did you throw Sara's bunny? That was not nice!"

"Because her bunny is ugly and I don't like it!" Ben said.

Mom shook her head. "Ben, that is not a good reason. You should not judge things by how they look. You should be kind and share with your sister. How would you feel if someone threw your truck and called it ugly?"

Ben thought for a moment. He felt sorry. He liked his truck and he did not want anyone to hurt it.

"I would feel sad and mad," Ben said.

"Then you should say sorry to Sara and give her bunny back," Mom said.

Ben nodded. He picked up Sara's bunny and walked to Sara. He gave her the bunny and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I was wrong. Your bunny is not ugly. It is cute and soft. Can we play together?"

Sara smiled. She wiped her tears and said, "Thank you, Ben. I'm sorry I called you mean. You are not mean. You are my brother. Can we play together?"

They hugged and went back to the hall. They played with their toys and had fun. They learned to be nice and respect each other. Mom was happy. She gave them a hug and a kiss. She said, "I'm proud of you, Sara and Ben. You are good children. You know how to say sorry and forgive. You know how to love."

Lily and Tom were sad. They did not want to leave the park. They wanted to have fun. They ran to the swings and pushed each other. They laughed and shouted. They did not see the raindrops falling.

Soon, the rain got heavier and heavier. It made loud noises on the ground and the trees. Lily and Tom got wet and cold. They were scared. They looked for Mom, but they could not see her. They did not know where to go.

Mom was looking for them too. She had an umbrella and a coat. She called their names, but they did not hear her. She was worried. She hoped they were safe.

Then, she saw them. They were hiding under the slide. They were shivering and crying. She ran to them and hugged them. She said, "I'm here, I'm here. Don't be scared. I love you." She gave them the umbrella and the coat. She said, "Let's go home. We can have some hot chocolate and cookies. And we can read a story."

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt better. They held Mom's hand and stepped out of the slide. They walked to the car. They did not mind the rain anymore. They were happy to be with Mom. They said, "We love you too, Mom. You are the best." Mom smiled and kissed them. She said, "You are the best too, Lily and Tom. You are my brave and sweet children."

Ben did come soon. He brought Lily's ball and her favorite treat. He was so happy to see Lily. He hugged her and kissed her. He said "You are a good dog, Lily. I'm glad you are better." One day, they found a bottle. It was big and brown and had a metal cap. Tom picked it up and shook it. He heard something inside. "What is it?" he asked Mia.

Mia looked at the bottle. It was dirty and had a label with words and pictures. She could not read the words, but she saw a picture of a skull and crossbones. She knew that meant danger. "It is bad," she said. "We should not open it. It might make us sick."

Tom did not listen. He was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He tried to twist the cap, but it was too tight. He used his teeth, but it hurt. He looked around and saw a big rock. He had an idea. "I can break it," he said. He ran to the rock and smashed the bottle on it.

The bottle broke with a loud noise. A dark liquid came out and splashed on Tom's face and clothes. It smelled bad and burned his skin and eyes. He screamed and dropped the bottle. Mia ran to him and tried to help. She saw the liquid on him and was scared. "Tom, Tom, are you okay?" she asked.

Tom was not okay. He felt pain and fear. He cried and wanted his mom. He wished he had listened to Mia. He wished he had not found the bottle. He wished he had not broken it. He learned a hard lesson. He learned that some things are better left alone.

"OK, but be gentle," Ben says. He lends Anna his hand. Anna puts her hand next to the flower. The beetle crawls onto her palm.

Anna smiles. She feels the beetle tickle her skin. She brings it close to her face. She says hello to the beetle.

"Hello, beetle. You are my friend. Do you want to play with me?" Anna asks.

The beetle does not answer. It flaps its wings and flies away. Anna and Ben watch it go.

"Bye, beetle. Thank you for playing with us," Anna says.

"Maybe it has to go home," Ben says.

Anna and Ben are sad. They miss the beetle. But they are still friends. They hug each other and go to play on the slide. They hope to see the beetle again.

Tom was a boy who liked to play outside. He had a red coat and a blue hat. He liked to run and jump and make snowballs. He had a friend named Sam who lived next door. They played together every day.

One day, Tom and Sam went to the park. They saw a big hill with white snow. They wanted to slide down the hill. They found a big piece of cardboard and put it on the snow. They climbed on the cardboard and held on tight.

"Are you ready?" Tom asked Sam.

"Yes, let's go!" Sam said.

They pushed the cardboard and it started to slide. It went faster and faster. They felt the wind in their faces and the snow in their hair. They laughed and shouted. They had fun.

But then, the cardboard hit a rock. It flipped over and threw Tom and Sam off. They landed on the snow. They were not hurt, but they were cold and wet. They looked at each other and saw their red noses and blue lips.

"Brrr, it's cold!" Tom said.

"I know, let's go home!" Sam said.

They got up and ran to their houses. They were tired from playing. They wanted to get warm and dry. They said goodbye to each other and went inside. They took off their coats and hats and put on their pajamas. They drank hot chocolate and ate cookies. They felt cozy and happy. They did not want to freeze anymore. They wanted to sleep. They had a good day.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a fancy car. It is big and shiny and has four doors. Sara and Ben run to the car and look inside.

"Wow, this car is so nice!" Sara says. "I wish I could ride in it."

"Me too," Ben says. "Maybe the owner will let us."

They knock on the window. A man opens the door. He is old and has gray hair. He smiles at Sara and Ben.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Do you like my car?"

"Yes, sir," Sara and Ben say. "It is very fancy."

"Thank you," the man says. "This car is very special to me. It was my youth car. I bought it when I was young and had fun with it. But now I have to part with it. I am moving to another place and I can't take it with me."

"That's sad," Sara says. "Where are you going?"

"I'm going to live with my son and his family. They have a big house and a farm. I will help them with the animals and the plants. I think I will be happy there."

"That's good," Ben says. "But what will happen to your car?"

"I'm going to sell it to someone who will take good care of it. Someone who will love it as much as I do. Maybe someone like you, when you grow up."

Sara and Ben look at each other. They both have a big dream. They hope that one day, they will have a fancy car like the man's. They thank him for letting them see his car and say goodbye. They run back to the park and play some more. They are happy and they are friends.

Tom and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells and rocks. Sometimes they found crabs and starfish too.

One day, they saw a man selling something from a big bucket. They went closer and saw that he had oysters. Oysters were animals that lived in shells. The man opened the shells and gave the oysters to people who paid him money.

"Mom, what are oysters?" Tom asked.

"They are a kind of food that some people like to eat. They are supposed to be delicious, but they are also very salty and slimy," Mom said.

"Can we try one?" Lily asked.

Mom looked at Dad and shrugged. "Sure, why not? It might be fun to try something new. But you don't have to eat it if you don't like it," she said.

She gave the man some money and he gave her two oysters. He also gave her a small fork and a lemon.

"Here you go, kids. This is how you eat an oyster. You use the fork to loosen it from the shell, then you squeeze some lemon juice on it, and then you slurp it down your mouth," he said.

He showed them how to do it and then smiled. "Do you want to try?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other and then at the oysters. They were curious, but also a little scared. They looked at Mom and Dad, who nodded and smiled.

"Okay, let's try," Tom said.

He picked up an oyster and did what the man said. He put it in his mouth and made a face. He did not like it at all. It was too salty and slimy and he spat it out.

"Yuck! I don't like oysters!" he said.

Lily saw Tom's reaction and decided to be brave. She picked up the other oyster and did the same thing. She put it in her mouth and closed her eyes. She liked it very much. It was juicy and tasty and she swallowed it.

"Mmm! I like oysters!" she said.

Mom and Dad laughed and hugged them. They were proud of them for trying something new.

"Good for you, Lily. You have a good palate. And good for you, Tom. You were brave to try it, even if you didn't like it. Maybe you will like something else better," Mom said.

"Can we have ice cream now?" Tom suggested.

"That sounds like a great idea. Let's go get some ice cream," Dad said.

They all walked to the ice cream shop and enjoyed their treats. Tom and Lily agreed that ice cream was delicious, even if they had different opinions on oysters.

In this episode, Timmy was trying to help his friends find their lost ball. Even though Timmy was slow, he knew he could help. He looked everywhere for the ball. Finally, he found it behind a big rock. Timmy's friends were so happy that they all clapped with Sally. They had a big party to celebrate, and everyone clapped and danced together.

When the caterpillar turned into a butterfly, it flew away and Shy felt happy that she could help. She realized that being shy was not always good and sometimes you need to be brave to help others. From that day on, Shy became more brave and made many new friends. The end.

"Let's draw on the blackboard!" Tim said. He picked up a white stick and wrote his name. Sam did the same.

They drew many things on the blackboard. They drew a sun, a house, a dog, a car and a smiley face. They had fun.

But then, they heard a loud voice. It was their teacher, Miss Lee. She was very angry.

"Tim and Sam, what are you doing?" she shouted. "That is not your blackboard. That is Mr. Brown's blackboard. He is the math teacher. He wrote important things on it. You erased them all!"

Tim and Sam felt scared. They dropped the white sticks and ran away. But they ran too fast. They did not see the big rock on the ground. They tripped and fell. They hit their heads. They felt dizzy and hurt.

Miss Lee came to them. She was still angry. She did not help them. She said, "You are very bad boys. You ruined Mr. Brown's work. You did not listen to the rules. You will go to the office. You will get in trouble. You will not play for a long time."

Tim and Sam cried. They wished they did not draw on the blackboard. They wished they did not run away. They wished they had a good friend to remind them to be good. But they did not. They had a bad day.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But they also liked to eat snacks. They had a bag of cookies that they shared.

"Can I have one more cookie?" Sam asked Mia.

"Okay, but only one. We have to save some for later," Mia said.

Sam took a big bite of the cookie. It was sweet and crunchy. He wanted another one. He looked at Mia. She was busy playing with a ball. He reached for the bag of cookies. He took another one. And another one. And another one.

Soon, the bag was empty. Sam felt full and sick. He threw the bag in the trash. He hoped Mia would not notice.

But Mia did notice. She came back to the bench where they left their snacks. She saw the empty bag.

"Sam, where are the cookies?" she asked.

Sam felt uncomfortable. He did not want to tell Mia the truth. He lied.

"I don't know. Maybe a bird took them," he said.

Mia looked at him. She saw the crumbs on his face and shirt. She knew he was lying. She felt angry and sad.

"Sam, you ate all the cookies. You did not share. That was not nice. You are a bad friend," she said.

She turned away from him. She did not want to play with him anymore.

Sam felt bad. He wished he did not eat all the cookies. He wished he did not lie to Mia. He wished he could say sorry. He regretted what he did. He wanted to be a good friend. He wanted to play with Mia again.

But Mia did not want to talk to him. She ignored him. She played with other kids.

Sam sat on the bench alone. He felt lonely and sorry. He learned a lesson. He learned to share and to tell the truth. He hoped Mia would forgive him. He hoped they could be friends again.

Ben and Sam were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them go fast and make loud noises. Ben had a red car and Sam had a blue car. They pretended they were racing on a big road.

"Vroom, vroom, I'm going to win!" Ben said.

"No, I'm going to win!" Sam said.

They pushed their cars harder and harder, until they crashed into each other. The cars broke into pieces and flew everywhere. Ben and Sam were very sad. They looked at their cars and cried.

"Look what you did!" Ben said, pointing at Sam.

"It's your fault!" Sam said, pointing at Ben.

They were very angry at each other. They started to shout and push and hit. They did not want to be friends anymore.

Their mom heard the noise and came outside. She saw the broken cars and the angry boys. She was not happy. She picked up the pieces and put them in a basket. She took Ben and Sam by the ear and pulled them inside.

"Ow, ow, ow, that hurts!" Ben and Sam said.

"You two need a time out!" Mom said. "You have to learn to share and be nice. And maybe, if you say sorry, I can fix your cars later."

She put them in separate corners and left them alone. Ben and Sam felt very bad. They looked at each other and felt sorry. They did not want to fight anymore. They wanted to play with their cars again.

They whispered to each other.

"Sorry, Ben."

"Sorry, Sam."

They hugged and made up. They waited for Mom to come back. They hoped she could reverse the damage and make their cars whole again. They promised to be careful and kind next time. They learned their lesson.

Sara liked to play with her toy box. It had many things inside that she could attach and detach. She could make cars, robots, animals and more. She had fun using her imagination.

One day, she found a new piece in her toy box. It was a knob. It was round and shiny and had a hole in the middle. Sara wondered what she could do with it. She looked around for something to attach it to.

She saw a wooden block that had a stick on one side. She thought it would be a good match for the knob. She tried to attach the knob to the stick, but it was too big. The knob fell off and rolled away. Sara was sad.

She looked for another piece that had a stick. She found a plastic cup that had a handle. She thought it would be a good match for the knob. She tried to attach the knob to the handle, but it was too small. The knob slipped off and bounced away. Sara was frustrated.

She looked for another piece that had a hole. She found a cardboard tube that had a hole on both ends. She thought it would be a good match for the knob. She tried to attach the knob to the tube, but it was just right. The knob fit snugly and stayed on. Sara was happy.

She had made a telescope. She looked through the tube and saw many things. She saw her mom, her dad, her dog and her toys. She saw the sky, the sun, the clouds and the birds. She saw the world. She smiled and said, "I love my knob!"

Sam liked to play with his toy laser. It was a red stick that made a bright light. He could point it at things and make them glow. He had fun with his laser, but he had to be careful. His mom told him not to shine it in his eyes or other people's eyes. She said it could hurt them and make them cry.

One day, Sam was playing with his laser in his room. He saw a big jar on his shelf. It was empty and clear. He wondered what would happen if he filled it with his laser light. He pointed his laser at the jar and pressed the button. The jar lit up like a firework. Sam was amazed. He moved his laser around and made different shapes and colors in the jar. He felt like a magician.

But then he heard a loud knock on his door. It was his dad. He sounded angry. He opened the door and saw Sam with his laser and the jar. He saw the harsh light coming from the jar. He was not happy. He took the laser from Sam and turned it off. He told Sam that he was being naughty and dangerous. He said that the laser could break the jar and make glass fly everywhere. He said that the light could hurt his eyes and his dad's eyes. He said that Sam had to go to time out and think about what he did.

Sam felt sad and sorry. He did not mean to be bad. He just wanted to fill the jar with his laser. He did not know it was wrong. He wished he had listened to his mom. He went to time out and cried. He hoped his dad would forgive him and let him play with his laser again. He promised to be more careful and not fill things with his laser. He learned his lesson.

Sam is clumsy. He trips over a rock. He spills the water. He falls on the sand. He hurts his knee.

Tim hears Sam. He runs to him. He sees his knee. He sees the blood.

"Don't cry, Sam," Tim says. "I can help you. I have a band-aid. I can put it on your knee."

"Thank you, Tim," Sam says. "You are a good friend."

They hug. They forget about the sand castle. They are happy.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But sometimes they get bored.

One day, they decide to crawl under the bed. They think it is fun and dark. They pretend they are spies. They whisper to each other.

"Shh, we have to be quiet. There might be monsters here," Tim says.

"I'm not scared of monsters. I have a big brain. I can outsmart them," Sam says.

They crawl deeper under the bed. They see a big box. They wonder what is inside. They open the box. They find a drum, a trumpet and a guitar. They are very happy. They want to make music.

They take out the instruments. They start to play. They make a lot of noise. They bang the drum, blow the trumpet and strum the guitar. They laugh and sing.

But their mom hears the noise. She comes to their room. She is not happy. She opens the door. She looks under the bed. She sees Tim and Sam with the instruments.

"What are you doing under there? You are making too much noise. You are supposed to be napping," she says.

"Sorry, mom. We were just playing. We found these instruments in the box. They are fun," Tim says.

"Well, they are not fun for me. They are giving me a headache. Put them back in the box and come out. You need to rest your brain and your ears," she says.

Tim and Sam obey their mom. They put the instruments back in the box. They crawl out from under the bed. They hug their mom and say sorry. They lie down on their beds. They close their eyes. They are quiet. They dream of music.

Jill likes jazz. Jazz is music with horns and drums and piano. Jill likes to dance to jazz with her dad. They spin and jump and clap. Jill is happy when she hears jazz.

But Jill's mom does not like jazz. She says jazz is too loud and too fast. She likes music with guitars and singers. She says jazz is cheap. She does not want to dance to jazz with Jill and her dad.

One day, Jill finds a jazz CD in her dad's car. She wants to play it at home. She puts it in the CD player and turns it on. She starts to dance. But her mom hears it and gets angry. She turns it off and takes it away. She says no jazz in the house.

Jill is sad. She wants to listen to jazz. She wants to dance with her dad. She does not understand why her mom does not like jazz. She tries to get the CD back. She struggles with her mom. She cries and kicks and screams.

Her dad comes home and sees them. He is surprised and worried. He asks what is wrong. He hugs Jill and her mom. He says they can listen to different music. He says they can dance to anything. He says he loves them both. He says jazz is not cheap. He says jazz is fun. He says jazz is for everyone. He puts the CD back in the player and turns it on. He asks Jill and her mom to dance with him. They do. They spin and jump and clap. They smile and laugh. Jill is happy. She likes jazz. She likes her dad. She likes her mom. She likes music.

Lila and Ben are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They are very happy with their snowman.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Lila says. "You are very big and smooth. Do you like the snow?"

"Yes, I do," Ben says in a funny voice, pretending to be the snowman. "But I am also very cold. Can you keep me warm?"

Lila and Ben think for a moment. How can they keep the snowman warm? They look around and see a pile of dry leaves. They have an idea.

"Let's make a fire!" Lila says. "We can use the leaves and some sticks. The fire will give heat and make the snowman cozy."

"Good idea!" Ben says. "But we have to be careful. Fire can be dangerous. We have to stay away from it and watch it."

They gather some leaves and sticks and make a small fire near the snowman. They see the fire crackle and glow. They feel the heat on their faces. They smile at each other and at the snowman.

"There, Mr. Snowman," Lila says. "Now you are warm and happy. Do you like the fire?"

"Yes, I do," Ben says in the funny voice. "But not too much. If the fire is too big, I will melt. Then I will be gone. And I don't want to be gone. I want to stay with you."

"Don't worry, Mr. Snowman," Ben says. "We will not let the fire get too big. We will keep it small and safe. And we will keep you company. We like you, Mr. Snowman. You are our friend."

Lila and Ben hug the snowman gently. They hear him laugh in the funny voice. They laugh too. They are happy with their friend. They play in the snow until it is time to go home.

"Ben, be careful with your fork!" Mom said. "Don't put it in your mouth. You might hurt yourself."

But Ben did not listen. He was too busy eating. He forgot about his fork and put it in his mouth. He felt a sharp pain and cried out loud.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Ben screamed. He dropped his fork and held his mouth. He had a red spot on his tongue.

Lily looked at Ben and felt sorry for him. She was not hungry anymore. She put down her fork and gave Ben a hug.

"I'm sorry, Ben. You are clumsy, but I love you," Lily said.

Mom got up and got some ice. She put it on Ben's tongue and kissed him.

"It's okay, Ben. It was an accident. You will be fine. Next time, remember your fork," Mom said.

Ben nodded and smiled. He felt better. He thanked Mom and Lily. He learned his lesson. He did not forget his fork again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Lily wore a pink apron and Ben wore a blue one. They had bowls, spoons, cups and some flour.

"Let's make a cake!" Lily said. "We need eggs, milk and sugar."

"OK!" Ben said. "I will get the eggs. You get the milk and sugar."

Ben opened the fridge and took out two eggs. He put them on the counter. He turned around to get a cup. But when he looked back, the eggs were gone!

"Hey, where are the eggs?" Ben asked. "Did you take them, Lily?"

Lily shook her head. She had the milk and sugar in her hands. She put them next to the flour.

"No, I didn't take them. Maybe they rolled away."

They looked under the table, behind the chairs, in the drawers. They could not find the eggs.

"Maybe they vanished!" Ben said. "Maybe a magic fairy took them!"

Lily gasped. She loved fairies. She looked around the kitchen, hoping to see one.

"Where are you, fairy?" she called. "Please give us back our eggs. We want to make a cake."

They heard a giggle from the window. They ran to see. There was a fairy sitting on the sill. She had a green dress, a pink hat and a wand. She had the eggs in her apron.

"Hello, children!" the fairy said. "I'm sorry I took your eggs. I was hungry and I wanted to make an omelet. But I see you want to make a cake. That sounds delicious. Here, you can have your eggs back. And I will help you with the cake. I have some magic sprinkles that will make it extra tasty."

Lily and Ben smiled. They thanked the fairy and invited her to join them. They cracked the eggs, poured the milk, added the sugar and the flour. They mixed everything well and put it in a pan. The fairy sprinkled some magic dust on top. They put the pan in the oven and waited.

Soon, the cake was ready. It smelled wonderful. It was golden and fluffy and had rainbow spots. Lily and Ben and the fairy cut a slice each and ate it. It was the best cake they ever had.

They were very happy. They thanked the fairy again and gave her a hug. The fairy said goodbye and flew away. She left the window open. Lily and Ben waved to her. They cleaned up the kitchen and put away their aprons. They decided to make another cake tomorrow. Maybe the fairy would come back.

"Be careful with the sauce, kids," Mom said. "Don't spill it or make a mess."

As Lily tried to keep the room tidy, she noticed that it was easier to find her toys and books. She also felt happy when she saw the tidy room. Her mom was proud of her, too. Lily learned that when you try to keep things tidy, it makes life easier and happier. And that was the moral value she learned: always try to keep things tidy, and good things will happen.

After a long time, Billy finished eating all the leaves. He was very happy because his broken horn was now fixed. He ran to his friends and showed them his horn. They all played together, jumping and running in the sun. And Billy was happy ever after.

One day, Bobo took a cookie from the kitchen when no one was looking. He felt guilty because he knew it was wrong. To make up for it, he decided to tell a joke to make everyone happy again. He said, "Guess what? Why did the cookie go to the doctor?" His friends laughed and guessed, "Because it was feeling crummy!" Everyone laughed, and Bobo felt better. As she gathered, the tide began to go out. Suddenly, she felt a spray of water on her face. She looked up and noticed a tall wave coming her way. Quickly, she gathered up her basket and ran away from the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. She had a pet cat and a toy car. Jane loved to play outside in her garden.

One day, Jane wanted to go for a dip in a pond in the garden. She quickly took off her shoes and socks, but she forgot to take off her pants. She jumped into the water and started to splash around.

Suddenly, Jane felt something on her leg. She looked down and saw a fake frog. It was wet and slippery. Jane was very scared.

Just then, her mum called. She quickly washed the fake frog off her leg. Then she put on her clothes and ran off to her mum. She told her mum about the fake frog, and her mum said it was only made of plastic. Jane was relieved and hugged her mum.

The moral of the story is that it's important to pay attention to what you are doing. Even if something appears to be real, it might be fake.

Once upon a time, Sam and his mum went to the airport. Sam was so excited, he wanted to get on the plane and go far away. But at the airport, something happened which made them feel embarrassed.

Sam's mum bent down and said, "Sam, stay here while I get our tickets. I want you to be a big boy and wait here." Sam nodded and said, "I can do it, Mum."

But after a few minutes, Sam got worried. He wandered away from his mum, to the other side of the airport. Sam wanted to find a special toy he'd seen. He was looking for it everywhere.

One night, the bunny heard a noise outside his den. He went to take a look, and saw a bear about to fall into cold water! The bunny knew he had to save the bear, so he quickly hopped to the edge of the water and grabbed him just in time!

The bear thanked the bunny for saving his life, and in return, he taught the bunny how to find food during the winter. With the help of the bear, the bunny stayed safe and warm until the winter was over.

The bunny was so thankful for the bear's help and he never forgot about the brave thing he did to save him!

The girl grabbed a wooden spoon and started stirring. Suddenly, a loud noise came from inside the dish. She jumped and stopped stirring. The kitchen was quiet, but the girl was still confused.

Just then, her mum walked in. She told the little girl not to worry, that the noise was just some cake dough she had been cooking. She smiled and said the cake was almost ready, and the girl could help her decorate it.

The girl was so happy to hear that - and so relieved to know what that loud noise was! She went back to stirring, and soon enough the cake was ready. The girl had so much fun helping her mum decorate it and was so proud when they finally cut into it.

The old lady smiled, happy that her plan was working. As the river rose and grew bigger, it flooded the lands around it. The townspeople were surprised at this strange sight--they had never seen anything like it before! 

As the river continued to rise, the old lady waved the stick one last time. Suddenly the river stopped rising and returned to its normal size. The townspeople cheered, grateful for the old lady's help. 

From then on, the townspeople called the old lady the "River-Rising Lady". They celebrated her every year, reminding themselves of the day the old lady and her long stick had magically made the river rise.

Days went by and the little crab kept watching the sailor come and go. One day, he saw the sailor drop something in the water. The little crab crawled over to investigate and found a shiny key!

The little crab knew that the key belonged to the sailor and he wanted to return it. So, he gathered all his courage and crawled into the water. He swam all the way to the boat and gave the key back to the sailor. The sailor was so grateful that he took the little crab on an adventure across the sea. And from that day on, the little crab wasn't afraid to be independent and go on his own adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside in the snow. One day, he found a big box on his doorstep. He was so excited to see what was inside that he quickly ran inside to unpack it. 

Inside the box, he found a toy igloo. He was so happy to have a new toy to play with. He went outside to play with it, but when he got outside, he saw that his best friend, Tommy, was already playing with his own toy igloo. 

Timmy was sad because he wanted to play with his new toy with his friend, but now they both had the same toy. He didn't know what to do. Tommy saw that Timmy was sad and offered to share his toy with him. Timmy was so happy that his friend was so kind and they both played with the igloos together.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big elephant. He was enormous! He liked to walk around the jungle and eat leaves from the trees. One day, he got an itch on his back and he couldn't reach it. So, he rubbed his back against a tree to make the itch go away.

Suddenly, the elephant heard a loud noise. It was the police! They were looking for a lost baby monkey. The elephant wanted to help, so he used his big nose to sniff around the jungle. He found the baby monkey and brought him to the police.

The police were very happy and thanked the elephant for his help. They gave him a big, shiny badge to wear on his trunk. The elephant was so proud and he rubbed his trunk against the badge to make it shine even brighter. From that day on, the elephant was known as the biggest and bravest helper in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to fly and sing all day long. One day, Tweet was flying over a farm when she saw a big bowl of seeds. Tweet was very hungry and wanted to eat the seeds, but she noticed a note next to the bowl that said, "Please don't eat all the seeds, save some for the other animals."

Tweet thought about the note and decided to only take a few seeds and leave the rest for the other animals. As she flew away, she felt happy that she did the right thing. 

Later that day, Tweet was flying over a smooth lake when she saw a group of animals gathered around a tree. She flew down to see what was happening and saw that the animals were all sharing the seeds from the big bowl. Tweet was happy to see that the other animals were able to eat too, thanks to her decision to only take a few seeds.

The moral of the story is that it's important to share and be kind to others. By sharing the seeds, Tweet made new friends and felt good about herself.

"Anna, Ben, come and eat your waffles. They are hot and sweet."

Anna and Ben groan. They do not want to eat. They want to sleep more.

"Mom, we are sleepy. Can we sleep more?" they ask.

"No, you cannot sleep more. You have to eat your waffles and then clean your room. You have too many toys on the floor. It is not safe." their mom says.

Anna and Ben sigh. They get out of bed and go to the kitchen. They see their waffles on the table. They smell good. They start to eat them. They feel a little better.

"Mom, these waffles are good. Thank you." they say.

"You are welcome. But remember, you have to clean your room after you eat. I will help you." their mom says.

Anna and Ben nod. They finish their waffles and go to their room. They see their toys everywhere. They feel a little tired. But they also feel a little happy. They like their toys. They start to pick them up and put them in their boxes. Their mom helps them. They sing a song while they clean.

"Clean, clean, clean the room. Make it nice and neat. Clean, clean, clean the room. Then we can have a treat." they sing.

Soon, their room is clean. They feel proud. They hug their mom.

"Mom, we did it. We cleaned our room. Can we have a treat?" they ask.

"Yes, you can have a treat. You did a good job. How about some ice cream?" their mom says.

Anna and Ben smile. They love ice cream. They run to the freezer and get some ice cream. They sit on the couch and eat it. They feel happy and full. They are not sleepy anymore. They are ready to play with their toys again. But this time, they will not make a mess. They will clean up after themselves. They learned their lesson. They love their mom. And they love their waffles.

Lily liked to draw with ink. She had many colors of ink and many papers to draw on. She liked to make pictures of flowers, animals, and stars. She was very good at drawing.

One day, Lily wanted to draw on the wall. She thought it would be fun and pretty. She took her ink and went to the wall in the living room. She started to draw a big sun with yellow ink.

But then, her mom saw her. She was not happy. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? You cannot draw on the wall. That is not good. That is not behaving. The ink will make the wall dirty and hard to clean. You have to draw on paper only. Do you understand?"

Lily felt sad. She did not mean to make her mom angry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to make a nice picture. I thought the ink was harmless. I won't do it again."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I know you did not want to be bad, but you have to follow the rules. The ink is harmless for paper, but not for the wall. Come, let's clean the wall together and then you can draw on paper as much as you want."

Lily nodded and helped her mom clean the wall. She learned her lesson and never drew on the wall again. She still liked to draw with ink, but only on paper. She made many beautiful pictures and gave some to her mom. Her mom was proud of her and loved her very much.

Lily and Tom were going on a journey with Mom and Dad. They packed their bags and got in the car. Lily was very excited. She wanted to see the animals at the zoo.

"Are we there yet?" she asked Mom.

"Not yet, sweetie. We have to drive for a long time. But you can look out the window and see the trees and the houses and the clouds," Mom said.

Lily looked out the window. She saw a big red truck and a yellow bus and a green bike. She saw a dog and a cat and a bird. She saw a bridge and a river and a hill. She saw many things, but she did not see the zoo.

She started to feel bored. She wanted to play with Tom, but he was sleeping. She wanted to read a book, but she left it at home. She wanted to watch a movie, but the car did not have a screen.

She sighed. She wished they were there already.

"Mom, can we stop and get some ice cream?" she asked.

"Sorry, honey. There are no ice cream shops available right now. We have to keep going. But I have a surprise for you. Do you want to know what it is?" Mom said.

Lily perked up. She loved surprises.

"Yes, please. What is it?" she asked.

Mom smiled. She reached into her bag and pulled out a small box. She handed it to Lily.

"Open it and see," she said.

Lily opened the box. Inside was a toy monkey. It had brown fur and a long tail and a funny face. It was wearing a hat and a shirt and a pair of glasses. It was holding a banana.

Lily gasped. She loved monkeys. They were her favorite animals.

"Wow! Thank you, Mom. It's amazing. What's his name?" she asked.

"You can name him whatever you want. He's your new friend. He can keep you company on the journey," Mom said.

Lily hugged the monkey. She decided to name him Bobo. She put him on her lap and talked to him. She told him about the zoo and the animals and the ice cream. She made him laugh and sing and dance. She forgot about being bored. She was happy.

She looked out the window again. She saw a big sign that said "Welcome to the Zoo".

"We're here! We're here!" she shouted.

She woke up Tom. She showed him Bobo. She grabbed her bag. She was ready to go.

She closed the box and put it in her bag. She did not want to lose Bobo. He was her new friend. He made the journey fun. She hoped he would like the zoo too.

Lily and Tom are human friends. They like to play in the park with their toys. One day, they find a big ball in the grass. It is red and shiny and bouncy.

"Wow, look at this ball!" Lily says. "Can I play with it?"

"Me too, me too!" Tom says. "I want to play with it!"

They both run to the ball and try to grab it. But the ball is too big for one human to hold. They pull and tug and shout.

"Mine, mine, mine!" Lily says.

"No, mine, mine, mine!" Tom says.

They are not peaceful. They are angry and loud.

A bird is watching them from a tree. It is blue and small and sings. It flies down to the ball and pecks it. The ball makes a hissing sound and goes flat.

"Oh no, oh no, oh no!" Lily and Tom say. "The ball is broken!"

They look at the bird. The bird looks at them. It tilts its head and says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet!"

Lily and Tom feel sorry. They realize they were silly and mean. They look at each other and say, "Sorry, sorry, sorry!"

They hug and smile. They are peaceful. They are happy.

They decide to share their other toys with each other and with the bird. They play together in the park. They have fun.

The end.

Lily liked to go outside at night and look at the stars. They were bright and shiny and made her happy. Sometimes she saw a shooting star and made a wish. She wished for a friend to play with.

One night, she heard a sound in the grass. It was a cricket. He was small and green and had long legs. He made a chirping noise with his wings. Lily was curious and went closer. She saw that the cricket had a light on his back. It was glowing like a star.

"Hello, cricket," Lily said. "Why do you glow?"

The cricket stopped chirping and looked at Lily. He was not afraid of her. He liked her voice.

"Hello, Lily," the cricket said. "I glow because I am special. I am an ancient cricket. I come from a faraway land where all the crickets glow. I can tell you stories about it, if you want."

Lily smiled. She wanted to hear stories. She liked stories. She sat down next to the cricket and listened. The cricket told her about his land, where there were many glowing things. There were glowing flowers, glowing fish, glowing birds, and glowing trees. It was a beautiful and magical place.

Lily and the cricket became friends. They talked and played and watched the stars. Lily was happy. She had found a friend to play with. She did not need to wish anymore. She had a glowing cricket.

One day, Lily sees a big book with a dragon on the cover. She wants to read it. She asks her mom to take it for her. Her mom says no. She says the book is too hard for Lily. She says Lily can pick another book.

But Lily insists. She says she wants the dragon book. She says she can read it. She says please. She says it again and again. She does not listen to her mom.

Her mom is not happy. She says Lily is being rude. She says Lily has to be gentle and polite at the library. She says Lily has to follow the rules. She says if Lily does not stop, they will go home.

Lily does not want to go home. She wants to stay at the library. She wants to read the dragon book. But she also wants to make her mom happy. She thinks for a moment. Then she says sorry. She says she will pick another book. She says she will be gentle and polite.

Her mom smiles. She says thank you. She says she is proud of Lily. She says they can read the dragon book together another day. She says they can find a book that Lily can read now. She says she loves Lily.

Lily hugs her mom. She says she loves her too. She says she is sorry for insisting. She says she will follow the rules. She says she is ready to pick another book. She says she still likes dragons.

Her mom is happy too. She says they can borrow the book. She says they can read it together at home. She says they can have fun. She says they can go to the library again soon.

They go to the counter. They show the book to the librarian. The librarian is gentle and kind. She says hello to Lily. She says she likes her book. She says she likes dragons too. She says she hopes Lily enjoys the story.

Lily smiles. She says thank you. She says she will enjoy the story. She says she likes the library. She says she likes the librarian. She says goodbye.

They leave the library. They walk to the car. They hold hands. They are happy. They have a book. They have a story. They have each other.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Tom said. "Do you want to be our friend?"

"Yes, please!" Lily said. "You look very nice and happy."

They hugged the snowman and smiled. They were having fun.

But then the sun came out. It was warm and bright. The snow started to melt. The snowman's hat and scarf fell off. His nose and eyes dropped to the ground. He became smaller and smaller.

"Oh no!" Tom said. "Mr. Snowman is going away!"

"Can we save him?" Lily asked. "Can we make him cold again?"

They tried to put the hat and scarf back on. They tried to find more snow. But it was too late. The snowman was gone.

They felt sad. They liked the snowman. They wanted him to stay.

But then they remembered something. They remembered how they made the snowman. How they laughed and played. How they hugged him and talked to him.

They looked at each other and smiled. They still had the memory. The memory of the snowman. The memory of their fun.

They held hands and said, "We will always remember you, Mr. Snowman. Thank you for being our friend. We love you."

They went inside. They were warm and cozy. They had a hot chocolate and a cookie. They told their mom and dad about the snowman. They showed them the pictures they took.

They were happy. They had a good day. They had a good memory. They had each other.

Her mom showed her how to make a star shape with her hands, and how to move them in the air. She said, "This is how we say hello to the stars. And this is how we say we love them." She made a heart shape with her hands, and put it on her chest.

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lila. You are my star."

Lia and Kai love to swim in the sea. They have a big boat with their mama and papa. They like to see the fish and the shells and the plants under the water. They have masks and fins to help them swim.

One day, they find a new place to swim. It is a reef. A reef is a big rock with many holes and colors. There are many different fish and animals on the reef. Some are big, some are small, some are bright, some are dark. Lia and Kai are very happy to see the reef.

They swim around the reef and look at everything. They see a starfish, a turtle, a clownfish, a crab, and a seahorse. They also see a big fish with a long nose and a stripe. It is a swordfish. The swordfish looks at them and swims away.

"Did you see that fish?" Lia asks Kai.

"Yes, I did. It was a swordfish. It has a sharp nose to catch food." Kai tells Lia.

"I like the swordfish. It is different from the other fish. It is fast and strong." Lia says.

"Me too. But we have to be careful. The swordfish can hurt us with its nose. We have to stay away from it." Kai says.

"OK. Let's swim to the other side of the reef. Maybe we can see more different things." Lia says.

They swim to the other side of the reef and have more fun. They see a coral, a sponge, a snail, and a jellyfish. They also see a big fish with a round mouth and a spot. It is a pufferfish. The pufferfish looks at them and puffs up.

"Wow, look at that fish!" Kai says.

"It is a pufferfish. It can make itself big and round to scare away enemies." Lia tells Kai.

"I like the pufferfish. It is different from the other fish. It is funny and cute." Kai says.

"Me too. But we have to be careful. The pufferfish can be poisonous. We have to stay away from it." Lia says.

"OK. Let's swim back to the boat. Maybe mama and papa have some food for us." Kai says.

They swim back to the boat and tell their mama and papa about the reef and the different fish they saw. Their mama and papa are proud of them and give them some sandwiches and juice. They eat and drink and talk about the reef. They are very happy. They love the sea and the reef and the different fish.

"Look, my boat is faster than yours!" Ben said, zooming his red boat past Anna's blue one.

"No, mine is faster!" Anna said, trying to catch up with him.

They were having so much fun, they did not hear their mom calling them for dinner.

"Anna! Ben! Time to eat!" Mom said, knocking on the bathroom door.

"Okay, Mom, we're coming!" Anna said, turning off the faucet.

She grabbed a towel and wrapped it around her. She looked at Ben and saw that he was still playing with his boat.

"Ben, come on, we have to go!" Anna said.

"But I want to play more!" Ben said, making his boat spin in the water.

"Mom will be mad if we don't go. And the food will get cold. And you'll be hungry. And you'll miss dessert. And you'll have to go to bed early. And you'll have bad dreams." Anna said, trying to remind him of all the reasons to stop playing.

Ben looked at her and frowned. He did not like any of those things. He was frightened of bad dreams. He loved dessert. He wanted to stay up late.

"Okay, okay, I'll go!" Ben said, putting his boat on the edge of the tub.

He grabbed another towel and wrapped it around him. He followed Anna out of the bathroom.

"Sorry, Mom, we were playing navy!" Ben said, smiling.

Mom smiled back and hugged them.

"That's okay, my little sailors. But next time, listen when I call you, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom, we will!" Anna and Ben said.

They sat down at the table and ate their dinner. They had soup and bread and cheese and salad and fruit and cake. They were very happy and full. They thanked Mom for the food and helped her clear the dishes. Then they brushed their teeth and put on their pajamas. They went to their bedroom and climbed into their beds.

"Good night, Anna!" Ben said.

"Good night, Ben!" Anna said.

They closed their eyes and dreamed of sailing on the big sea.

"Look, Mom, look, Dad, the otters are so cute!" Lily said.

"Yes, they are, honey. Do you know what they have on their fur?" Mom asked.

Lily shook her head. She did not know.

"They have thick fur, Lily. Thick fur keeps them warm and dry in the water. Can you say thick fur?" Mom said.

"Thick fur, thick fur," Lily repeated.

"Very good, Lily. How about you, Ben? Do you know what the otters eat?" Dad asked.

Ben nodded. He knew.

"They eat fish, Dad. Fish are yummy. Can I have some fish?" Ben said.

"Maybe later, Ben. But you can't feed the otters, okay? They have their own food. Can you guess what they use to crack open the shells of the fish?" Dad said.

Ben thought for a moment. He looked at the otters. He saw something shiny in their paws.

"Is it a rock, Dad? Do they use a rock?" Ben guessed.

"That's right, Ben. They use a rock. They are very smart animals. Can you say smart animals?" Dad said.

"Smart animals, smart animals," Ben repeated.

"Very good, Ben. You are both very smart, too. Now, let's watch them for a little while, and then we can go see the other animals, okay?" Mom said.

Ben and Lily nodded. They watched the otters with Mom and Dad. They were happy.

But then, something bad happened. One of the otters saw Ben's hat. It was a red hat with a big star on it. The otter liked the hat. It wanted the hat. It jumped out of the water and ran to the fence. It grabbed the hat with its teeth and ran back to the water.

"Hey, that's my hat! Give it back, otter!" Ben shouted.

He tried to reach the hat, but the fence was too high. He could not get it. He saw the otter swim away with his hat. It put the hat on the rock and hit it with another rock. It tried to crack open the hat like a shell.

"Stop, otter, stop! You are breaking my hat!" Ben cried.

He was very sad. He liked his hat. It was his favorite hat. He did not want the otter to have it.

"Ben, I'm sorry, honey. The otter took your hat. It doesn't know that it's yours. It thinks it's a toy. Maybe we can get it back later, okay?" Mom said.

She hugged Ben and tried to calm him down.

But Ben was not okay. He was angry and sad. He did not like the otter anymore. He did not like the zoo anymore. He wanted to go home.

He stomped his feet and screamed.

"I hate the otter! I hate the zoo! I want my hat!" Ben yelled.

He made a big fuss. He made everyone look at him. He made Mom and Dad very upset.

They had to leave the zoo. They did not see the other animals. They did not have fun.

It was a bad day. It was a bad ending.

Sara was angry and did not listen to Ben. She grabbed his car and ran away. Ben was sad and chased after her. He wanted his car back. He shouted at Sara and tried to take his car, but Sara was faster. She ran into the kitchen and saw a switch on the wall. She did not know what it was, but she thought it looked unusual. She pushed the switch and hoped it would make Ben go away.

But the switch was not a toy. It was for the oven. When Sara pushed it, the oven turned on and became very hot. Sara did not notice, but she put Ben's car on top of the oven. The car started to melt and smoke. Sara smelled something bad and saw the car. She was scared and dropped the car. It fell on the floor and made a loud noise.

Ben heard the noise and ran into the kitchen. He saw his car on the floor, all melted and burned. He was very angry and sad. He cried and yelled at Sara. He said she was mean and he hated her. He said he would never forgive her for ruining his car.

Sara felt sorry and wanted to say sorry. She did not mean to hurt Ben or his car. She just wanted to play. She tried to hug Ben and tell him she was sorry, but Ben pushed her away. He did not want to talk to her or play with her. He ran to his room and slammed the door. Sara was left alone in the kitchen, feeling sad and guilty. She wished she had not pushed the switch. She wished she had shared with Ben. She wished Ben would forgive her. But he did not.

One day, they see a new toy in the park. It is a big, red car. It has four wheels, a horn and a steering wheel. It looks very original and cool.

Lily and Ben both want to play with the car. They run to it and try to get in. But the car is too small for both of them. They start to push and pull each other. They are not nice to each other.

One day, they saw a new boat in the harbor. It was red and shiny and had a funny name. They wanted to see it better, so they walked along the pier. They forgot to remind each other to be careful. They forgot to look where they were going.

Suddenly, Tom tripped on a rope and fell into the water. He was scared and cold and wet. He cried for help. Lily was worried. She ran to the boat and shouted for help too. She hoped someone would hear them.

A man came out of the boat. He saw Tom and Lily and heard their cries. He was kind and brave. He threw a life ring to Tom and pulled him out of the water. He wrapped him in a warm blanket and gave him a hug. He told Lily not to worry. He said he would take them to their mom.

Tom and Lily were happy and grateful. They thanked the man and said they were sorry. They said they would never forget to remind each other to be careful again. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that the harbor was fun, but also dangerous. They learned that they had to listen to their mom and to each other. Tom says, "This is my flag. I am the king of the garden. You have to do what I say." He puts the flag on a stick and waves it in the air.

Sam says, "No, this is our flag. We can share it. We are both kings of the garden. You have to be nice to me." He tries to grab the flag from Tom.

Tom and Sam start to fight over the flag. They pull and tug and shout. The flag rips in half. Tom and Sam stop fighting. They look at the flag. They feel sad and sorry.

They hear a loud noise. It is their dad. He comes out of the house. He sees the flag. He is angry. He says, "What have you done? This is a famous flag. It is very old and special. It belonged to your grandpa. He fought in a big war with this flag. He was brave and strong. He gave it to me. And you tore it apart. You are very naughty."

Tom and Sam tremble. They are scared of their dad. They say, "We are sorry, dad. We did not know. We were playing. We did not mean to hurt the flag. Please don't be mad at us."

Dad sighs. He says, "I know you did not know. But you have to be careful with things that are not yours. You have to respect them. And you have to respect each other. Fighting is not good. Sharing is good. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sam nod. They say, "We understand, dad. We are sorry. We love you. We love each other. We love the flag. Can you fix it?"

Tom and Sam hug their dad. They say, "We promise, dad. We can do that. Thank you, dad. You are the best dad in the world."

Dad hugs them back. He says, "You are the best sons in the world. Now, let's go inside and have some cookies. And maybe later, I will tell you more about your grandpa and his famous flag."

Once upon a time, there was a wise old cat. This cat had a very long tail. One day, the cat was walking down a path when it saw a little mouse.

The wise cat thought for a moment. Then it said, "I will use my long tail to help you find your way home." So the cat walked in front of the mouse, and the mouse held onto the cat's tail.

As they walked, the wise cat and the little mouse saw a big dog. The dog wanted to chase them. The wise cat knew they had to act fast. "Hold on tight!" the cat said to the mouse. The cat then began to reverse, pulling the mouse with its tail.

The dog tried to follow, but the wise cat was too fast. The cat and the mouse were safe. They kept walking until they found the mouse's home. The little mouse was very happy and thanked the wise cat for helping.

Once upon a time, there was a slow dog named Bob. Bob loved to jog every day. He jogged in the park, near the big tree, and by the pond with the ducks.

One day, Bob saw a man with a bottle of wine. The man was not careful and dropped the bottle. The wine spilled all over the ground. Bob did not know what wine was, so he went to sniff it.

Bob sniffed the wine, and he felt very funny. He tried to jog, but he could not. He was too dizzy from the wine. Bob fell down and could not get up. His owner found him and was very sad.

The moral of the story is to be careful and not to touch things you do not know.

Once upon a time, there was a long spike. The long spike lived in a big forest. In the forest, there were many trees and animals. The long spike was friends with all the animals.

One day, the long spike met a small bird. The bird was sad. The long spike asked, "Why are you sad?" The bird said, "I can't fly high. My wings are too short." The long spike wanted to help the bird.

The long spike had an idea. It said, "I can be your wings. Hold on to me, and I will help you fly high." The bird held on to the long spike, and they flew high in the sky. The bird was happy, and they became best friends. They played and had fun together every day in the big forest.

One day, a little bird came to sit on the bean plant. The bird was lost and needed help. The wise old man talked to the bird and showed it the way home. The bird was very thankful and flew away happily. The wise old man and the bean plant became best friends and they lived happily ever after.

But then she heard a loud voice. It was Mom. She came into the kitchen and saw Daisy on the table. She was very angry.

"Daisy, what are you doing?" Mom shouted. "You are a very naughty dog! You ate our breakfast and made a big mess! You have to go outside now!"

Daisy felt sorry. She knew she did a bad thing. She jumped off the table and ran to the door. She looked at Mom with sad eyes.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Daisy said. "I was very hungry and the food smelled good. I love you, Mom."

Mom sighed. She loved Daisy, too. But she was still angry.

"I love you, too, Daisy," Mom said. "But you have to learn to behave. You can't eat our food and make a mess. You have to wait for your own food and eat in your bowl. Do you understand?"

Daisy nodded. She understood. She went outside and waited for Mom to give her some food. She hoped Mom would forgive her. She decided to be a good dog from now on.

Tom is a boy who likes to help on the farm. He likes to feed the cows and the pigs and the chickens. He likes to give them hay and corn and water. He likes to see them happy and full.

One day, it is very hot and sunny. Tom goes to the barn with a bucket of water. He sees the cows and the pigs and the chickens. They are thirsty and tired. They need water to drink and cool down. Tom gives them water from the bucket. He pours some on the ground and some in the troughs. He sees them drink and splash and play. He likes to see them happy and wet.

But Tom forgets something. He forgets to close the barn door. He leaves it open when he goes back to the house. He does not see the wind blow and the clouds come. He does not hear the thunder and the rain. He does not know that the water is coming to the barn.

The water comes to the barn. It comes fast and hard. It fills the barn with mud and puddles. It makes the hay and the corn and the water wet and dirty. It makes the cows and the pigs and the chickens sad and cold. They need dry and clean things to eat and drink and sleep. They do not like the water in the barn.

Max's owner took off his leash and let him run around. Max was so happy that he ran and played without being scared anymore. From that day on, Max knew that whenever he felt scared, he could just dance and forget all his worries.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max was very obedient and always listened to his owner, Sarah. One day, Sarah took Max on a trip to the city. They rode on a big train that went underground. Max was scared at first, but he was very brave and didn't bark.

When they arrived at their stop, Sarah and Max got off the train. Max was so happy to be outside again, he wagged his tail and ran in circles. Suddenly, a little girl came up to them and said, "Hi, can I pet your dog?" Sarah said, "Yes, of course you can." Max was happy to make a new friend.

As they walked around the city, Max saw lots of new things. He saw tall buildings, bright lights, and lots of people. Max was very tired by the end of the day, but he was happy he got to go on an adventure with Sarah. When they arrived back home, Max fell asleep right away, dreaming of all the fun he had that day.

Years later, Lily met a boy named Jack. They fell in love and got married. They used a special ring just like Lily's mommy and daddy. They promised to always be kind to each other and to never give up on their marriage. 

Lily learned that love is important, but being kind and never giving up is even more important.

The father and son went on their trip and ended up at a lake. Sam saw the lake and said, "Let's go for a walk around the lake!" The son agreed and he walked with Sam. Suddenly, Sam stopped walking and said, "Do you remember the pole I gave you earlier?" Confused, the son shook his head. 

Sam smiled and said, "Let's put the pole we have here to use. Give it a try and you will see!" 

The son didn't understand what Sam meant, but decided to give it a try. He moved the pole around in the lake and soon came up with a huge fish! Sam smiled and said, "See, it can be so useful!" From then on, the son always takes the pole with him whenever they go on trips.

Once there was a bald old man who wanted to teach a little girl to go. But the girl was scared and did not want to go. The old man tried to show her all the fun she could have if she went to the park, but she was still scared. So the old man decided to go with her. 

When they got to the park, the little girl started to explore and her fear turned to joy. She ran around, played and laughed with all the other children. The old man was content to watch and teach the little girl all about exploring and having fun.  

Soon, the little girl conquered her fear of going and loved adventuring. The old man was so proud of her and always reminded her that even bald old men should not be afraid to go out and enjoy life.

Once upon a time there was a loyal dog named Leo. Leo was very excited to go on an adventure, and he knew just where to go!

He ran and ran until he came to a cave. The cave was full of clay and it was very soft under his paws.

Leo was a brave and loyal pup, so he decided to explore the cave. He sniffed around and soon found a tunnel. He followed the tunnel, feeling his way through the dark.

Suddenly he saw a glimmer of light at the end of the tunnel and he ran towards it. He found himself in a secret room full of treasures. He was so excited that he wanted to explore further.

Suddenly he heard a voice.

"Who are you?" it asked.

Leo was a bit scared, but he answered. "I'm Leo, and I'm loyal. I'm exploring this cave," he said.

The voice laughed. "I'm the owner of this cave. You can stay here as long as you like if you promise to be loyal. But first you must lead me through the tunnel to the secret room!"

Leo agreed, and he quickly led the owner of the cave through the darkness. When they reached the secret room, the owner was amazed.

Leo had been brave, loyal and clever, and his reward was to be allowed to stay in the cave and explore! From that day

Once upon a time, there was a small boat on a huge lake. The lake was very big and rough and the boat was filled with people. They were all worried because they could not get to the other side. Suddenly, a strong wind started to blow and the waves got even bigger.

The people on the boat began to panic, but one little girl had an idea. She told them to all pray to the wind and to the lake, asking them to stop pushing the boat. Then she grabbed an anchor and threw it into the lake.

The little girl's actions worked and the wind calmed down and the waves became smaller. Finally, the little girl's anchor held the boat in place and they were able to get to the other side of the lake safely.

The people in the boat were so happy with the girl's bravery and resourcefulness. She taught them that when things look the most hopeless, you should never give up. You should try your best to stay strong and you can always find a way to make things better.

One day, a boy and his dad went to the park. The boy saw a big mushroom. He wanted to spray it.

"Dad, can I spray it?" The boy asked.

"Yes, but be creative," his dad said.

The boy smiled. He lifted up the spray can and started to spray the mushroom. He sprayed it yellow and then brown. He added some red and blue. He sprayed the mushroom in creative patterns and shapes.

When he finished, he stood back and smiled. He looked at the mushroom and he was very proud of his work. It looked like a beautiful piece of art.

The boy laughed and said, "Thanks Dad. This is the best mushroom I ever made!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was only three years old and just starting to talk. Every day, Amy and her mom would walk to the park and look at the animals.

One day, when they arrived at the park, Amy saw something she'd never seen before. It was a big bull! She pointed at it and asked her mom: "What's that?".

Her mom smiled and said: "That's a bull, Amy".

Amy thought that the bull was very available, so she went up to it to have a closer look. She cautiously reached out her hand to pet the bull, but it started to move away from her. Amy's mom laughed and said: "It looks like he doesn't want to be petted right now".

Amy thought about it for a moment and then asked: "Can I come back and pet him later?".

Her mom nodded and said: "Yes, I'm sure you'll be able to pet him when he's more available".

And so, Amy and her mom walked away, happy with the thought that the bull would soon be available so that she could pet it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lola. She loved to play with her toys in her room. One day, when she was playing, she saw a cake on the table. She couldn't believe her luck! She quickly ran over to it and grabbed it with her hands. 

Suddenly, she felt a pinch on her arm. It was her Mom! She had been watching Lola the whole time. Lola was very frightened, her face became pale. Mom said sternly, "Lola! You can't take the cake without permission! You have to be more careful next time." 

Lola knew this was a lesson she wouldn't forget. She was very fearful and quickly put the cake back down. She promised herself to always ask for permission before taking things. 

The next day, despite being worried, Lola grabbed the cake once again. When she touched it, the same pinch came back, even stronger than before. It was Mom again! This time, she scolded Lola for not following her order and took the cake away from her. Lola was denied from eating the cake, and sadly went back to her room with a heavy heart.

Once there was a farmer who had a hay field. Every day the farmer would shear the hay and bring it to his barn. One day, while the farmer was working, the sky suddenly turned gloomy. The farmer said to the sky, "What's wrong?" 

The sky said to the farmer, "I'm sad. There is too much hay growing in your field and it's blocking my sun."

The farmer thought about it for a moment, and then he said, "I know what I can do. I can harvest all the hay before it grows too tall. Then the sun can shine through again." 

And so the farmer worked diligently all day to harvest the hay. When the farmer was finished, the sky smiled and said, "Thank you! Now I'm happy again." 

The farmer smiled and said, "It's no problem. I want to make sure you are happy." 

The sky beamed with joy, and the farmer went back home, happy that he could help the sky.

One day, John and Kate had a look outside their house. It was a kind day, and the sun was shining brightly. They decided to go for a walk. 

John and Kate had a lot of fun. They laughed and ran around until they saw a thing they'd never seen before. It was a strange creature. 

John and Kate looked at each other and asked, "What is that?" 

The creature replied in a low, gruff voice, "I have come to take you away!" 

John and Kate had never been so scared. They shouted for their parents, but no one heard them. The creature grabbed John and Kate and flew away. 

John and Kate had a bad ending to their kind day. They never returned to their happy home, and no one ever knew what happened to them.

Once there was a tall tree. Its leaves were big and green. Every day a little girl came to play under it. She played all kinds of games like tag and hide and seek.

One day the little girl got an idea. She asked her mom for a spade so she could bury something in the ground. Mom gave her a spade and a prune. So the little girl took the spade and prune and started digging a hole in the ground.

When the little girl was done digging the hole, she put the prune inside and started to bury it. She quickly patted down the soil and said out loud, "I buried a prune!" 

Mom smiled and said to the little girl, "Well done! You buried the prune in a very good spot." The little girl smiled and thanked her mom. 

The little girl dug up her buried prune the next day and was surprised to find that it was all dried up! The little girl was so proud of her work. She ran back to the tall tree, where Mom was waiting for her. 

Mom hugged the little girl and said, "I'm so proud of you! You buried that prune so well!"  The little girl smiled and hugged her mom back. She was so proud of her accomplishment.
